# Wazza OS user guide: the full text

> Wazza OS runs desktop apps (GIMP, Blender, Inkscape, ONLYOFFICE, a browser and others) in virtual machines on your Linux computer, each app in a tab with its own AI agent (a Chat) that works in that app. This user guide explains every capability: install and first start, tabs and apps, Chats, agents and models, several agents at once, Drive (agents that see and use an app's screen), Computer Control, skills, files between your computer and the VMs, the Wazza OS MCP for outside agents (Claude Code, Codex and others), the command line, every setting, privacy, memory and troubleshooting.

Every page of https://os-guide.wazza.ai/ in menu order, as markdown. The index of pages: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/llms.txt

Wazza OS is for Linux. Install it with one command in a terminal: `curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh`

# Wazza OS

AI that works with you, in the tools you already use. Wazza OS runs a computer of its own (a virtual machine) next to yours, with real desktop apps in it, and AI agents that work in those apps beside you: you ask, they work, you watch, step in, or carry on in your own tab.

- **Real apps, safely apart.** GIMP, Blender, ONLYOFFICE, a browser, VSCodium and dozens more run in virtual machines, not on your computer.
- **Several agents at once.** Each app opens in a tab with its own Chat; agents work in parallel tabs while you keep yours.
- **Skills and personas.** Agents load know-how for each app and task, and learn your way of working.
- **Drive.** Agents see the app's screen and use the mouse and keyboard, in any app.
- **Any AI.** A plan you already pay for, an API key from one of 73 providers, a company gateway, or a model on your own computer.

- **Runs on**: Linux: Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, openSUSE, Arch (x86-64, with KVM)

- **Install**: One command (or one package); the VM is created and managed for you

- **Agents**: Hermes, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity

- **Models**: Your plans, your API keys (73 providers), any compatible API, or a Wazza OS account

## Install

Paste this in a terminal, on the Linux computer where Wazza OS will live. It asks for your password once, for `sudo`.

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh
```

To test first, without installing anything:

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --check
```

### Finds your package type

Debian, Ubuntu and their family get the `.deb`. Fedora and openSUSE get the `.rpm`. Arch and its family get the Arch package. Any other distribution gets the tarball.

### Verifies the release

Nothing installs unless the release manifest carries Wazza's Ed25519 signature and the package matches its signed SHA-256 and size.

### Resumes if cut

The package is large. If the download stops, run the command again: it continues where it stopped.

What your computer needs, other ways to install, updates and removal: [Install, update, remove](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html). Your first start, step by step: [The first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html).

## Connect your AI agent

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, Gemini CLI, Hermes and Prime Agent can work in Wazza OS through `wazza-os mcp`, the MCP server that comes with it. For Claude Code, once:

```
$ claude mcp add --scope user wazza-os -- wazza-os mcp
```

The line for each agent: [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html#connect-an-agent-from-outside). Everything an agent can do: [Every Wazza OS MCP tool](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html).

## Control Wazza OS

- **From a terminal**, on your desktop or on a server: [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html), and [Wazza OS on a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html) (with its own virtual screen).
- **From an agent**: [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html) and [Every Wazza OS MCP tool](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp-tools.html).

## How it fits together

Three words carry the whole manual: **the VM**, **tabs** and **Chats**.

- **The VM** (virtual machine) is a complete Ubuntu computer that Wazza OS starts, sizes and stops for you. Apps are installed in it, not on your computer, so they never touch your own files unless you hand them over. You can have up to 8 VMs (4 running at once); most people use one, `vm-1`.
- A **tab** shows one app of the VM (GIMP, Blender, a browser, the VM's file manager…) in the Wazza OS window. Tabs work like a browser's: open as many as you like, switch, close.
- A **Chat** sits beside each app, in its tab. You write to an **agent** (the AI program that works for you) and it works in that tab's app: through the app's own tools, or by looking at the app's window and using its mouse and keyboard ([Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html)). A Chat can also start other agents in other tabs.

[Getting around](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html) shows the window part by part; [Glossary](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/glossary.html) defines every word.

## Capabilities

Each card says what the capability is, why or when you would use it, and who it is for. The link opens the full page: how to do it step by step, every option, the limits and examples.

[

### Several agents at once, each in its own app

WhatOne Chat hands parts of a job to other agents, each in its own app tab (a browser for research, GIMP for images, an editor for code), all working at the same time.

WhyEvery agent has its own window, mouse and keyboard: none waits for a shared screen, and you watch any of them, or keep using your own tab, without getting in the way.

WhoAnyone with a job that spans several apps: research plus a report, assets plus a game, data plus slides.

Several agents at once → ](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html) [

### One install, the VM managed for you

WhatOne package for your distribution. Wazza OS creates its VM, sizes its memory, processors and disk by itself, starts it with the app and keeps itself up to date with signed updates.

WhyA complete Linux desktop with apps and agents, without setting up a VM, drivers or a container.

WhoEveryone: no virtualization knowledge needed.

Install, update, remove → ](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html) [

### Real desktop apps, with your graphics card

WhatAbout 70 ready-to-install apps: Blender, FreeCAD, Godot, GIMP, Inkscape, Kdenlive, OBS Studio, ONLYOFFICE, Chromium, VLC, VSCodium and web apps (Google, Microsoft, social networks). 3D apps draw on your GPU (Vulkan, OpenGL, OpenCL).

WhyUse the plan you already pay for (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google), your own API keys, or a free model, in the same window.

### Drive: agents see and use app windows

WhatAn agent looks at its tab's app as a picture and clicks, drags, types and presses keys in it, like a person, for every app, even one with no tools of its own.

WhyAny desktop app becomes something an agent can operate, and you see every action happen.

WhoAnyone who wants an agent to do GUI work: edit an image, fill a form, set up a scene.

### Computer Control: an agent on your real computer

WhatA special Chat that can see and use your own computer's screen, keyboard and mouse, after you allow it, until you stop it or close its tab.

WhyFor work outside the VM: an app installed only on your computer, your own desktop settings.

WhoExperienced users who understand what they allow; never needed for work in the VM.

### Skills that improve from your Chats

WhatSkills are written know-how agents load (how to use GIMP, how to write a report). Wazza OS ships many, reviews your Chats to learn lessons and new skills, and lets you read, edit and add them, and group them into personas.

WhyAgents get better at your apps and your way of working, and what one Chat learns, the next one knows.

WhyYour files go into the VM only when you say so, and come back as new files, never over yours.

### Memory, processors and disk, handled for you

WhatThe VM takes memory when its apps need it and gives it back when idle, within a limit you can set (by default 75 % of the memory free); processors and disk follow the same rule.

WhyYour computer stays responsive; heavy work gets what it needs.

## What's new in this release

**Wazza OS 0.3.1** (build 344048ba2f7d, published 2026-11-27): a lighter download with a smaller VM image that keeps your files from 0.3, Wazza OS shown as one process, one Applications page that fills your screen for every VM, and many fixes to Chats, apps, tabs and updates. Every change is on [What's new](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/whats-new.html); the main ones:

- The VM image is smaller, so the download is lighter. When you update from 0.3, your files, Chats and settings in the VM come over to the new image ([The Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html)).
- One **Applications** page for all your VMs, filling the window, with a right-click menu everywhere and each running VM's CPU and memory on it; with two or more VMs, every tab shows which VM it belongs to ([Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html)).
- The Wazza OS window resizes from every edge and corner, and Wazza OS shows as one process, **wazza-os**, in your system monitor ([The window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html), [Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html)).
- [Settings › General › Web browser](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html): one choice of browser for every web app and every web link.
- Kdenlive downloads the first time you open it, every app install shows its download moving, and an app tab always shows its own app while it starts.
- Many fixes to Chats, sign-in, updates, tabs and Settings: see [What's new](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/whats-new.html).

### Known limits in this release

- Memory: with one Chat open, Wazza OS and its VM still use more of your computer's memory at rest than we aim for; making it smaller continues in the next updates ([Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html)).
- An agent on your computer (Claude Code, Codex and the other harnesses that run outside the VM) does not close a tab with unsaved work either, but it may not get the warning yet: its close can end with a time-out instead ([Several agents at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html#limits)).
- After **Keep open**, an app may still show its own "save changes?" question, and Wazza OS may ask again: choose **Cancel** in the app's question to keep working (being fixed).
- Until the next update, don't press × again while a tab's Chat is saving its work (after **Save** in the question, or with **Always save** remembered): Wazza OS can then end the app while it asks you, and work the Chat did not save yet is lost. An agent's forced close at the same moment can do the same. Being fixed.
- An agent in the VM cannot install Zed or Wave Terminal for you yet: install them from their card in **Apps**.
- To change **Opens a file** on an app you already added, add the app again ([Fill the form](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html#fill-the-form)): Edit app keeps the setting it was added with.
- A tab that comes back with a document you cannot read (its permissions) opens its app on it, and the app says what it can; Wazza OS does not yet say why. For a document that is gone or was moved, Wazza OS says so. A tab that comes back in the background, behind the tab you are on, does not do this yet: if its document is gone, was moved or cannot be read, the tab shows **Could not open** with a technical reason, and its app does not start (being fixed).
- For the apps whose own installer replaces the program in place: an app you start yourself inside the VM (from a Desktop tab's dock, or as a command in a terminal) while that same app's update is installing does not wait for the update yet, so it can start while its program is being replaced. An app tab waits for it ([When an app updates](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#when-an-app-updates)); if such a start misbehaves during an update, close it and start it again.

## About this manual

- Written for **Wazza OS 0.3.1** (build 344048ba2f7d, published 2026-11-27). The screenshots come from a test computer (Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME) running Wazza OS 0.2.0: alpha 2 and the builds that followed it, whose screens are the same.
- Press `/` anywhere to search every page and heading; the search works offline.
- The sun and moon button switches between dark (the default, like the app) and light.
- Words in **bold** are what Wazza OS shows on screen: a button, a tab, a menu item. Home › Sign in › API keys means: open Home, then Sign in, then its API keys tab.

# Quick start

From nothing to an agent working in an app, in about ten minutes: install, start, give your agents a model, ask a first question, then let an agent work in an app while you watch.

## 1. Install Wazza OS

Paste this in a terminal, on the Linux computer where Wazza OS will live. It finds your package type, checks the release's signature and installs it; it asks for your password once, for `sudo`:

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh
```

To test first, what your computer needs, or a package to download yourself: [Install, update, remove](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html).

## 2. Start it

Open **Wazza OS** from your app menu. The first start shows six short steps (about two minutes): click **Get started**, check that every line of the computer check says *ok*, skip or fill the sign-in and agent steps, keep the default apps, and click **Set up Wazza OS**, then **Open Wazza OS**. Each step in detail: [The first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html).

![The first start's welcome card with Get started](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-1-welcome.webp)

## 3. Give your agents a model

Agents think with an AI model, which someone pays for. Pick one way (you can add the others later):

- **A plan you already pay for** (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google): Home › Sign in › Logins › **Log in with …**.
- **An API key**: Home › Sign in › API keys › **+ Add key** on the provider's card, paste the key, **Check and save**. An OpenRouter key opens hundreds of models, some of them free.
- **A Wazza OS account**: Home › Sign in › **Email and password**.

![Sign in, API keys tab, the OpenRouter card open with its Paste API key field and Check and save](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/signin-add-key.webp)

Adding an OpenRouter key: paste it, then **Check and save**.

Details: [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).

## 4. Ask a first question

1. Click **+** at the end of the tab strip, then **Chat** (*Ask any agent*).
2. Type a request and press `Enter`. Try one that makes the agent work in the VM: *Create a file named hello.txt in my Documents folder with today's date in it, then show me its content.*

![The agent ran a command in the VM, created the file and showed its content](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-answer.webp)

The agent ran a command in the VM (the *Bash* row), made the file and showed it.

The agent works in the VM: it can make files, run commands and use the web there, without touching your own computer. Everything about Chats: [Chats, agents and models](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html).

## 5. Let an agent work in an app

1. Click **+**, type *gimp* in **Search apps**, click **GIMP**. It installs (a minute or so), then opens in a new tab with its own Chat on the left.
2. In that Chat, ask: *Create a new 800 x 600 image with a dark teal background and write Hello from Wazza OS in large white letters in the middle.*
3. Watch GIMP on the right: the agent uses GIMP's own tools, then checks the result.

![The agent's answer and the image in GIMP with Hello from Wazza OS on a dark teal background](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/drive-gimp-result.webp)

More: [Apps and tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html), and how agents use an app's window: [Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html).

## 6. Go further

[

### Several agents at once

One request, several apps, each with its own agent working at the same time.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html) [

### Files and sharing

Bring your files into the VM and get results back on your computer.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html) [

### Skills

What agents know about each app, and how they learn from your Chats.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html) [

### Settings

Theme, resources, defaults for new Chats, and every other option.

Read →](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html)

# Install, update, remove

Wazza OS installs with one command on any recent Linux, or as a package of your distribution. Start it from your app menu, and it sets up the rest (its VM, its apps, its agents) on its first start.

## What your computer needs

| Need | Why |
|---|---|
| Linux on a 64-bit Intel or AMD processor (x86-64), with glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 and later, a current openSUSE Tumbleweed or Arch) | Wazza OS is built for it. |
| Hardware virtualization (Intel VT-x or AMD-V) turned on, so `/dev/kvm` exists | The VM runs only with KVM. Most computers have it; on some it must be turned on in the firmware settings (UEFI/BIOS). |
| A desktop session with systemd (GNOME, KDE, Xfce, Hyprland, Sway…), and XWayland on Wayland desktops | Wazza OS's window and the VM's panes are X11 windows. On a server with no desktop, see [On a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html). |
| Memory: 8 GB works (the computer of this manual's screenshots had 8 GB); 16 GB or more is comfortable for 3D apps and several agents at once | The VM takes memory as its apps need it and gives it back; Wazza OS always keeps 2 GB and 10 % of your memory for your computer itself ([Memory, CPU and disk](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/memory-cpu.html)). |
| Disk: about 8 GB for Wazza OS itself, plus room for the VM's disk (it grows as you use it, by default up to half of your free space) | The package holds the VM's system image. |
| A graphics card with its driver (Intel, AMD, or NVIDIA 495 or newer) | Apps in the VM draw on it. Without one the VM still works, with slower software graphics. |
| An Internet connection | For agents' models, installing apps in the VM, updates. |

After installing, `wazza --check` says exactly what your computer has and what is missing ([What is checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#what-is-checked)).

## Install with one command

Paste this in a terminal, on the Linux computer where Wazza OS will live. It asks for your password once, for `sudo`.

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh
```

To check your system first, without installing Wazza OS (only the few tools the installer itself uses, such as `curl` and `zstd`, are installed when they are missing):

```
$ curl -fsSL https://os.wazza.ai/install.sh | sh -s -- --check
```

| It… | How |
|---|---|
| finds your package type | Debian, Ubuntu and their family get the `.deb`. Fedora and openSUSE get the `.rpm`. Arch and its family get the Arch package. Any other distribution gets the tarball. |
| verifies the release | Nothing installs unless the release manifest carries Wazza's Ed25519 signature and the package matches its signed SHA-256 and size. |
| resumes if cut | The package is large (about 6 GB). If the download stops, run the command again: it continues where it stopped. |

It needs free disk for the package plus about 1 GB, and checks before it starts. It downloads into `/var/tmp/wazza-install` and leaves the package there (delete it to free the space); to use another folder, put `WAZZA_INSTALL_DIR=/some/big/folder` before `sh`. To choose the package type yourself, add it after `--`: `sh -s -- tar` (or `deb`, `rpm`, `arch`). When it is done, start Wazza OS from your applications menu.

> You install Wazza OS only once. After the first install, it updates itself from the [Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html): it checks for a new signed version every hour, and installing it is two clicks and your administrator password.

## Install a downloaded package

The install command leaves the package it downloaded in `/var/tmp/wazza-install` (or the folder you gave it). To install that package yourself, or one copied from another computer, use your system's package manager:

### Ubuntu and Debian

```
$ sudo apt install ./wazza-*.deb
```

Write the `./` in front: it tells apt to install that file, and apt installs what it needs with it (bubblewrap, ffmpeg, Openbox, Xvfb and the other dependencies).

### Fedora

```
$ sudo dnf install ./wazza-*.rpm
```

### openSUSE

```
$ sudo zypper install ./wazza-*.rpm
```

### Arch and Arch-based systems

```
$ sudo pacman -U ./wazza-*.pkg.tar.zst
```

### Any other Linux (tarball)

```
$ tar --zstd -xf wazza-*.tar.zst
$ cd wazza-os-*/
$ ./install.sh --check
$ sudo ./install.sh
```

`./install.sh --check` only lists what your system is missing (the commands and libraries Wazza OS needs: systemd, util-linux, Python 3, Xvfb, xauth, Openbox, D-Bus, FFmpeg, bubblewrap, slirp4netns, iproute2, OpenSSL, Git). Install those with your package manager, then `sudo ./install.sh` puts the files where the packages put them. It refuses while something is missing (`--force` installs anyway).

### What the packages bring

Each package installs what Wazza OS needs with it. One more piece is GStreamer's PipeWire plugin, with which [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html) sees a Wayland screen. GNOME usually has it already. On a KDE Plasma or a minimal system, Wazza OS installs it after each update from Wazza OS's Update page. Only that one package is installed: your system is never updated with it, and if it cannot be installed then, the update still ends well and Computer Control names the command when you open it ([If the card says it cannot see your screens](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html#screens-plugin)):

| Your system | Package |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu, Debian | `gstreamer1.0-pipewire` (recommended: apt installs it with Wazza OS) |
| Fedora | `pipewire-gstreamer` |
| openSUSE | `gstreamer-plugin-pipewire` |
| Arch | `gst-plugin-pipewire` |

With the tarball installed by hand (`sudo ./install.sh`), install it yourself to use Computer Control on KDE Plasma; Computer Control names the command when it is missing. Its next update from Wazza OS's Update page installs it too.

## Start Wazza OS

Open **Wazza OS** from your app menu (Activities, the application launcher, or the start menu of your desktop). Or, in a terminal of your desktop session, run one of these (they are the same program):

```
$ wazzaos
```

`wazza-os` and `wazza` work too. Only one Wazza OS runs per user: starting it again while it runs goes to the one already running. The very first start shows six setup steps: [The first start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html).

### Move to a new computer

To take your VM with you: on the old computer, back up vm-1 ([Settings › Virtual machines](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#backups), **Back up** on its row) and copy the zip from Downloads to the new computer. Install Wazza OS there, then on its first start click **Start from a backup…** and pick the zip: vm-1 starts as it was, with the setup skipped ([The first start › Start from a backup](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html#start-from-a-backup)).

## Update Wazza OS

Three ways, all keep your VMs, Chats, sign-ins and settings:

- **From Wazza OS**: Home › Update shows a new version as soon as it is out (it checks every hour); click **Download Update**, then **Install Now** ([The Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html)).
- **With your package manager**: install a new package file (the install command leaves the one it downloads in `/var/tmp/wazza-install`) exactly as above, over the installed one (`sudo apt install ./new.deb`, `sudo dnf install ./new.rpm`, `sudo pacman -U ./new.pkg.tar.zst`, or the new tarball's `sudo ./install.sh`). Then quit and start Wazza OS.
- **With the install command**: run it again ([Install with one command](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html#install-with-one-command)): it installs the newest version over yours. Then quit and start Wazza OS.

> **Never uninstall to update**
>
> Removing the package deletes your Wazza OS data (below). To update, or to go back to an older version, install the other package over the one you have.

Going back to an older version is a downgrade: Debian and Ubuntu do it with `sudo apt install --allow-downgrades ./older.deb`; Fedora with `sudo dnf downgrade ./older.rpm`; Arch with `sudo pacman -U ./older.pkg.tar.zst`.

## Remove Wazza OS

> **Removing Wazza OS removes your Wazza OS data too**
>
> Every package's removal stops Wazza OS and its VMs, then deletes Wazza OS's data on this computer: the VMs' disks (and every file you made inside them), Chats, sign-ins and keys, settings, caches. Your own files outside Wazza OS (Documents, Downloads, Desktop…) stay, including `Downloads/From the VM` and VM backups. Back up a VM you want to keep first ([Virtual machines › Backups](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#backups)).

| System | Command |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu, Debian | `sudo apt remove wazza-os` |
| Fedora | `sudo dnf remove wazza-os` |
| openSUSE | `sudo zypper remove wazza-os` |
| Arch | `sudo pacman -R wazza-os` |
| Tarball | `sudo ./uninstall.sh` (in the unpacked folder) |
| Any of them | `sudo wazzaos --uninstall`: removes Wazza OS with the system that installed it (apt, dnf, zypper, pacman or the tarball's uninstaller), naming each folder it deletes with its size |

To erase Wazza OS's data but keep it installed (a fresh start), use [Settings › This computer › Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-all-data) instead.


---

Page: The first start (Start here)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/first-start.html

# The first start

The very first time you open Wazza OS, six short steps check your computer, offer to sign you in, ask which AI agents you use, let you pick your first apps and set up Wazza OS's own computer (its virtual machine). It takes about 2 minutes. Every later start takes about 1 minute and goes straight to your tabs.

- **When**: Only on the very first start of Wazza OS for your user account

- **How long**: About 2 minutes, most of it the VM's first boot

- **What you need**: Wazza OS installed and started from your desktop session ([Install](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/install.html))

- **Can I change it later?**: Yes: everything you pick here is in Home › Sign in and Home › Apps

Every step except the first has **Back**: you go to the step before with every choice kept. Nothing you pick in these steps is final, and you can skip everything that is optional (signing in, the agent logins, the extra apps): Wazza OS works without them, and you add them later.

![The Wazza OS window on its first start: the welcome card in the middle of an empty dark window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-1-window.webp)

The first start in the Wazza OS window. While you go through the steps, Wazza OS already starts its virtual machine in the background, so the last step is often almost done when you reach it.

## Step 1: Welcome

The first card says what Wazza OS is: your apps and AI agents, in a computer of their own. Wazza OS runs its own Linux computer (a virtual machine, "the VM") next to yours. Agents work there, in your apps, with you, and they ask before anything reaches your real computer.

![Step 1 of 6: Your apps and AI agents, in a computer of their own, with the Apps, Agents and Safe tiles and the Get started button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-1-welcome.webp)

Step 1 of 6.

1. The counter and the six bars at the top show where you are: **First start · step 1 of 6**.
2. Click **Get started**.

The three tiles sum up what you get: **Apps** (office, browser, creative, developer apps and more, installed in the VM), **Agents** (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes and more, working in those apps) and **Safe** (your files are copied into the VM only when you say so; see [Privacy and security](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/privacy-security.html)).

## Step 2: Checking this computer

Wazza OS checks, in a few seconds, the six things it needs to run its VM next to your computer. Each line shows what it found and **ok**, **limited** or **missing**. When something is not right, the line says what it means and how to fix it (a command to run, or a setting).

![Step 2 of 6: Checking this computer, a list of checks each marked ok: Hardware virtualization (KVM), systemd user session, X11 display (XWayland), Chat sandbox, Graphics driver, VM display buffers](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-2-check.webp)

Step 2 of 6 on a computer where everything is present. The list scrolls: the sixth check, VM display buffers, is below the fifth.

1. Each check has a mark: **✓** present, **!** limited (Wazza OS works with less), **✕** missing (something does not work until you fix it).
2. Its state in words on the right: **ok**, **limited** or **missing**.
3. Click **Continue** once the check has answered (the button stays grey while it runs).

### What is checked, and what to do when a line is not ok

| Check | Why Wazza OS needs it | When it is missing: the fix the check gives |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware virtualization (KVM) | Wazza OS's VMs run only with KVM. Without it they do not start. | Turn on Intel VT-x or AMD-V (SVM) in the computer's firmware settings (UEFI/BIOS), then restart. If `/dev/kvm` exists but your account cannot open it: `sudo usermod -aG kvm "$USER"`, then log out and back in. If the module is not loaded: `sudo modprobe kvm_intel` or `sudo modprobe kvm_amd`. Inside a VM: turn on nested virtualization in the computer that runs it. |
| systemd user session | Each VM runs in a memory-capped scope of your user's systemd manager. | Start Wazza OS from your desktop session (log in through the login screen), not from `su`, `sudo` or a bare SSH session. On a server: `loginctl enable-linger "$USER"` keeps your user manager running without a login (see [On a server](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli-server.html)). |
| X11 display (XWayland) | The Wazza OS window and the VM's panes are X11 windows; in a Wayland session that is XWayland. Without a display Wazza OS does not open (on a server, Wazza OS makes its own virtual screen). | Install your distribution's XWayland package, turn XWayland on in your compositor (Hyprland: `xwayland { enabled = true }`; Sway: `xwayland enable`), then log out and back in. |
| Chat sandbox | Every Chat that runs on your computer (not in the VM) runs inside Wazza OS's sandbox (bubblewrap and Landlock), or does not start. | On Ubuntu: `sudo apparmor_parser -r /etc/apparmor.d/wazza-bwrap` loads Wazza OS's AppArmor rule. If the kernel refuses user namespaces: `sudo sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=1` (and the same line in `/etc/sysctl.d/60-wazza-userns.conf` to keep it). If the sandbox file is missing: reinstall Wazza OS. *Limited* means Chats run under Landlock alone, with less isolation. |
| Graphics driver | The VM draws its apps on your computer's graphics card. Without a usable card the VM starts with software graphics (slower), by itself. | Intel and AMD: the kernel's driver (i915/xe, amdgpu) with Mesa; NVIDIA: its driver 495 or newer with `sudo modprobe nvidia-drm`. If the card exists but your account cannot open it: `sudo usermod -aG render "$USER"`, then log out and back in. Or set [VM resources › Graphics › GPU](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#graphics) to **None (CPU only)**. |
| VM display buffers | The VM's picture travels over a socket that needs 4 MiB buffers. Below that, VMs do not start. | `sudo sysctl -w net.core.rmem_max=4194304 net.core.wmem_max=4194304`. The package installs `/usr/lib/sysctl.d/60-wazza.conf`, which sets it at every boot; reinstall Wazza OS if that file is missing. |

You can run the same check at any time: [Settings › This computer › Check](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#check), or in a terminal `wazza --check` (see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#check)).

> **Continue works even when a line is missing**
>
> The first start does not stop you. But a *missing* line means that part does not work (for example no KVM: the VM does not start). Fix it first, then click **Continue**.

## Step 3: Sign in to Wazza OS (optional)

A Wazza OS account keeps your Chats, skills and settings in sync between computers, and gives your agents Wazza OS's own models (Prime Agent uses them; new Chats start on MiMo once you are signed in). You can skip it and sign in later in [Home › Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html#your-wazza-os-account).

![Step 3 of 6: Sign in to Wazza OS, with Email and password, Log in / Sign up online, Back and Skip for now](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-3-signin.webp)

Step 3 of 6.

1. **Email and password** opens the sign-in form below the buttons, for an account you already have.
2. **Log in / Sign up online** asks where to open the website's sign-in (for a Google account, or to create an account).
3. **Skip for now** goes on without an account. The note at the bottom left reminds you: *You can sign in later in Home › Sign in*.

### Sign in with email and password

![The sign-in form with the Email and Password fields and the Sign in button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-3-email.webp)

1. Type your account's email.
2. Type your password (Enter also signs in).
3. Click **Sign in**. The card says *Signing in…*, then *Signed in.*, and the next step comes by itself. A wrong password or a network problem is shown in red under the form, in the server's own words; the password field is emptied every time.

### Log in or sign up online

![Where should it open? In the VM's browser (offered once the VM is ready) or On this computer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-3-online.webp)

1. **In the VM's browser**: the website's own sign-in page opens in Wazza OS's private sign-in tab, where you log in or sign up with your email or Google; you are signed in by itself. The VM must be running for this, so during the first start the button says *Offered once the VM is ready*. When you pick it, the card notes that *the online sign-in opens in Wazza OS's private sign-in tab once your computer is set up* and goes on to the next step.
2. **On this computer**: your own browser opens Wazza OS's Google sign-in. When you land on the last page, copy its address from the browser's address bar and paste it in the field Wazza OS shows, then finish. To sign up or log in with an email instead, do it on the website, come back, and use **Email and password**.

## Step 4: Which agents do you use? (optional)

If you already pay for an AI plan, Wazza OS can use it: you log in once and your agents use your plan, with no API key. This step only notes which logins you want; each one opens after the setup, in Home › Sign in.

![Step 4 of 6: Which agents do you use? Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Google, OpenRouter and Nous Portal, each with a Log in with button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-4-agents.webp)

Step 4 of 6.

1. Click **Log in with …** for each plan you have. The button turns into **✓ After setup**; click it again to take it back.
2. Click **Continue**.

| Login | Plan it uses | Which agents can use it |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Free, Pro or Max plan | Claude Code only |
| ChatGPT | Plus or Pro plan | Every agent: Codex, Hermes and Prime Agent with their own sign-in; Claude Code and Antigravity through Wazza OS's gateway |
| Grok | SuperGrok or X Premium+ | Every agent |
| Google | Your Google account plan | Antigravity only |
| OpenRouter | Your OpenRouter account | Every agent |
| Nous Portal | Your Nous Portal account | Hermes only |

The card also says *Hermes and Prime Agent work right away*: they need no login of their own. They still need a model to talk to: a Wazza OS account, one of these plans, or an API key. The published Wazza OS includes no shared key, so without any of the three a Chat has no model; see [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).

## Step 5: Pick your first apps

The apps you check here are installed in the VM while it starts. You can install any other app later from [Home › Apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#install-an-app).

![Step 5 of 6: Pick your first apps, a grid of apps; Git, GPU for apps, OSM places and routes, Search and Sound card drivers are already checked](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-5-apps.webp)

Step 5 of 6. The grid scrolls: every app of the catalog is in it.

1. The apps with a light border are Wazza OS's own defaults: they are always installed and cannot be unchecked (Git, GPU for apps: Vulkan, OpenCL and OpenGL support, OSM places and routes, Search, Sound card drivers; Wazza OS also installs the ffmpeg media tools with them).
2. Click any other app to add it (click again to take it back).
3. The number of apps in the catalog (71 in this version).
4. Click **Set up Wazza OS**.

> Each app you add takes time and disk space in the VM. Pick only what you will use today: every app stays one click away in Home › Apps.

## Step 6: Setting up your computer

The last card follows the VM's start, stage by stage, each with the time it took.

![Step 6 of 6: Setting up your computer, five stages each with a check mark and its time, and the Open Wazza OS button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/first-start-6-setup.webp)

Step 6 of 6, all stages done. Here the system's first boot took 1 min 27 s; it was running while the steps before were on screen.

The stages, in order:

  - **Getting ready**: Wazza OS prepares the VM's disk and settings.
  - **Starting the virtual machine**: the VM is switched on.
  - **Starting the system**: the VM's Linux boots (the longest stage on a first start).
  - **Starting the desktop**: the VM's desktop, where your apps draw, comes up.
  - **Connecting Wazza OS**: Wazza OS connects to the VM (its files, apps and Chats).
2. Click **Open Wazza OS**. Before the VM is ready the button says *Opens when your computer is ready…*: click it anyway and Wazza OS opens by itself as soon as it is.

Wazza OS then opens [Home](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#home) on **Apps**, or on **Sign in** when you picked a sign-in or a login in steps 3 and 4 (each login you picked waits there for you). The apps you picked keep installing in the background; each one sends a notification when it is done ([Home › Notifications](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#notifications)).

## Start from a backup

On a new computer (or after [Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-data)) you can start Wazza OS from a VM backup you made before, a vm-1 already set up with your apps, files and settings, instead of setting up a new one. The setup is skipped: the backup's VM starts as it was.

1. On step 1, click **Start from a backup…** (left of **Get started**). A file window opens: **Choose a Wazza OS VM backup**. Pick the backup's zip and click **Choose**. To make a backup on your old computer: [Settings › Virtual machines › Backups](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-vms.html#backups).
2. The card asks **Start from this backup?** and says what the zip holds (the VM it was made from, when, its size). Click **Start from this backup**, or **Back** for the normal first start.
3. **Starting vm-1 from your backup**: the new vm-1 this first start began is stopped at once, the backup is read and checked, its disk takes vm-1's place and vm-1 starts on it. Steps 2 to 5 are skipped: the backup's VM brings its own apps and files. Your Wazza OS account and your API keys belong to this computer, not to the VM: add them afterwards in [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).
4. **Starting your computer from the backup** follows vm-1's start, then **Open Wazza OS** opens it, as in step 6.

Wazza OS refuses, in plain words, a zip that is not a Wazza OS VM backup and a backup made on another base image (another version's VM system): the Welcome comes back with *Not started from …* and why, and **Get started** goes on with the normal first start. If the backup's disk does not start, the new vm-1 is put back, and the Welcome says so the same way.

From a terminal, on a new computer, start Wazza OS from a backup directly: `wazza --vm1-backup ~/backups/wazza-vm-1-2026-11-04-1200.zip` (see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#start-from-a-backup)). The first start then shows no steps: only **Starting vm-1 from your backup**, then **Open Wazza OS**.

## After the first start

- Every later start shows only the startup card (the stages of step 6) and then your tabs as you left them.
- Open a Chat and talk to an agent: [Quick start](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/quick-start.html).
- Connect a model if you skipped steps 3 and 4: [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html).

## Run the first start again

To see the six steps again without losing anything, run this in a terminal while Wazza OS is open, then quit and start Wazza OS:

```
$ wazza --gui setup reset-first-run
first start not done: Wazza OS shows its first start at its next start
```

Your VMs, Chats, apps and sign-ins stay. To start from nothing instead (every VM, Chat, sign-in and setting erased), use [Settings › This computer › Remove all data](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-computer.html#remove-data).

On a computer you set up from a script (or many computers), `wazza --gui setup run --file setup.json` does the same choices without clicks: see [The command line](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#set-up-without-clicks).


---

Page: Getting around (Start here)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html

# Getting around

The Wazza OS window has a tab strip at the top and the tab you are on below it. One tab is special: Home, with its menu on the left (Apps, Settings, Sign in, History, Update, Notifications, Feedback). Every other tab shows one app of the VM with its own Chat beside it.

## The window

![The Wazza OS window on Home, Apps page: the tab strip at the top, the Home menu on the left with the account card and the VM card at its bottom, and the Apps catalog on the right](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/home-apps-full.webp)

Home open on Apps, right after the first start.

1. **Explorer**: opens the side panel with the VM's files ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-explorer)).
2. **Tabs**: one per open app (and Home). Click one to show it; drag one to move it.
3. **+** (**Show apps**): opens Home on Apps, to open or install an app.
4. **Desktop menu**: fold the Chat or the app, lock input, pop out, full screen, frame rate ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-desktop-menu)). Grey on Home, where there is no app.
5. **Window buttons**: minimize, maximize, close. Closing the window quits Wazza OS and stops its VMs (your tabs come back at the next start).
6. **Home menu**: Apps, Settings, Sign in, History, Update, Notifications (with the number of unread ones), Feedback. Below 1024 px of width it becomes a column of icons.
7. **Account card**: *Not signed in*, or the Wazza OS account you are signed in with. A click opens Sign in.
8. **VM card**: the VM this window shows, live ([below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#the-vm-card)).
9. **The page** of the Home menu item you picked (here Apps).

To resize the window, drag any of its edges or corners: the cursor changes to a resize arrow where you can drag.

## Home

Home is the tab of Wazza OS itself. It opens on the page you pick in its menu; each page opens in the same Home tab (the tab's name follows the page: Applications, Settings, Sign in…).

| Home menu item | What it is | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Apps | Every app you can open or install, by category, with search and **Add app** | [Apps and tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html) |
| Settings | Eight pages of settings | [Settings](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html) |
| Sign in | Your Wazza OS account, plan logins, API keys, custom APIs, web apps | [Sign in](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html) |
| History | Your past tabs and Chats, to search and reopen | [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#history) |
| Update | A newer version of Wazza OS | [The Update page](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html) |
| Notifications | Everything Wazza OS told you | [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#notifications) |
| Feedback | Tell the Wazza team what went wrong | [below](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#feedback) |

### The VM card

The card at the bottom left of Home, live while Home is open:

- the VM's name and state (*vm-1 · running*);
- **CPU**: how busy the VM's processors are;
- **RAM**: the memory the VM uses, of the most it may take now (*0.9 / 5.8 GB*);
- how that limit is set (*Auto: 75% of the memory free now, never below 5.8 GB, so 5.8 GB now*; see [VM resources › Memory](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-resources.html#memory));
- the graphics the VM's apps get (*OpenGL 4.2 · virgl (…)*: your graphics card, through virtualization).

## Tabs

A tab shows one app of the VM, with its Chat beside it: the agent of that Chat works in that app. Tabs keep running when you switch away: an app keeps working and its agent keeps going in the background.

![A GIMP tab: the Chat on the left with its composer and the agent and model chip, GIMP on the right](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-tab-layout.webp)

A GIMP tab, just after GIMP was installed and opened.

1. The tab, named after its app, then after the first thing you ask its Chat.
2. The tab's **Chat** ([Chats, agents and models](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html)).
3. The divider: drag it to give the Chat or the app more room. Which side the Chat is on is a setting ([General › Chat side](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#tabs-and-layout)).
4. The **app**, live from the VM. Click into it and use it as on your own computer: your mouse and keyboard go to the app while the pointer is over it. Your computer keeps its own `Super` key: for the VM's, which opens Wazza OS's app launcher for that VM (the page a new tab shows; until this update it typed `Super` into the VM, where nothing answered it), press `Ctrl`+`Alt`+`Space`, then let go; to send `Ctrl`+`Alt`+`Space` itself to the app (Blender's fullscreen area, for one), press `Space` twice while holding `Ctrl` and `Alt`. You can turn this off ([General › Keyboard](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#keyboard)).
5. The composer, where you write to the agent.
6. The agent and model this Chat uses (a click opens the model window).

### Open, switch and close tabs

- **Open**: click **+**, then an app on the Apps page (or ask a Chat to open one). An app that is not installed yet installs first, then opens ([Install an app](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/apps.html#install-an-app)).
- **Switch**: click a tab. A tab an agent opened in the background carries a badge until you look at it.
- **Close**: the **×** on the tab. Its app is asked to close. When it has unsaved work, Wazza OS asks you what to do: **Close without saving**, **Save** (the tab's Chat is asked to save it; in a tab without a Chat, **Save in** the app focuses the app for you to save) or **Keep open**. Tick **Remember my choice** in that question to answer every later close the same way, with no question: **Save** then always has the tab's Chat save first, **Close without saving** always closes without saving. **Keep open** is never remembered. Change it in [Settings › General › Unsaved work](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#unsaved-work). On a Desktop tab, **Close without saving** ends every app started from that tab's dock (even one whose window you moved elsewhere) and every other app whose windows are all in that tab. An app started elsewhere that also has a window outside the tab (in another tab, on every desktop, or in a window no tab shows) keeps running with its work, and Wazza OS names it once the tab is closed. An app Wazza OS could not end keeps the tab open, and Wazza OS says which one and why: save or close it there, then close the tab again. After **Close without saving** (chosen in the question or remembered), the tab stays where it is and shows **Closing…** until its app has really ended; then it goes. An app that has not ended about 30 seconds later is ended the ordinary way. If it cannot be ended, the tab says why: close it again.
- **Reopen**: a closed tab is in [History](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#history).

### The tab card

![The card shown when hovering a tab: its title, GIMP, VM vm-1, Shown, RAM 174 MB, CPU 0% (app 130 MB, Chat 44 MB), and a small picture of the tab](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-tab-hover.webp)

Hold the pointer over a tab: a card shows its full name, its app and VM, what it uses now (memory and CPU, split between the app and its Chat) and a small picture of it.

### The tab menu

![The tab menu opened by a right-click on a tab: Add to favourites, Reload, Move to new window, Group: Add tab to new group, Sound: Mute tab and Volume 100%](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-tab-menu.webp)

Right-click a tab:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| Add to favourites | Keeps the tab in History › Favourites, to reopen it in one click. |
| Reload | Restarts the tab's app (when it stopped answering, for example). |
| Move to new window | Moves the tab into a new Wazza OS window; its app and its Chat go on there. |
| Group › Add tab to new group | Puts the tab in a named, coloured group (type a name, pick a colour); the group's own menu adds tabs or **Ungroup**s them (they stay open). |
| Sound › Mute tab, Volume | Only what you hear from this tab. An agent working in it still hears the app. Only the tab you are on is heard. |
| Close tab | (on tabs that can be closed) Closes it; its app is asked to close. |

### When a VM or Wazza OS starts again

Your tabs come back, like your apps after a restart of your computer (unless you turned **Restore tabs after a restart** off in [Settings › General › Tabs & layout](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#tabs-and-layout): then after a restart your apps don't come back and open fresh when you open them; your Chats stay). When a VM starts again (after **Stop**, after you quit and start Wazza OS, after a crash or a restart of your computer), every tab of it reopens and its app starts again with its project, if the project was saved: in your home folder, or on a shared folder of your computer, a second disk or a removable drive (`/mnt`, `/media`). Apps that restore themselves do so: Chromium reopens its pages, VSCodium and Zed their windows. An app you or a Chat added ([Add your own apps](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/custom-apps.html)) reopens its file when it opens files (**Opens a file** ticked, or, with it off, when its launch script is one plain `exec` line of a program whose own desktop entry opens files, as a start from the dock does); otherwise it starts without the file, and its tab says so. Apps you started yourself inside a tab (from the dock of a Desktop tab, for example) start again in it, with their saved project, when that tab starts again; an app running on no tab (its tab was closed, or it shows on every desktop) starts again with the VM's first Desktop tab (else its first app tab other than Chromium); on a VM with no tab at all it is not started again. After a crash, each tab reopens with the project Wazza OS last noted for it: it notes it when you leave the tab, when the window loses focus, and every 5 minutes while you work in it or a Chat answers. The tabs of a VM you do not look at reopen too, in the background, one app after another while that VM has the memory for them; an app that cannot start yet waits, and starts when you show that VM.

**Stop** and quitting Wazza OS close the apps first, the same way as closing a tab: each tab whose app has unsaved work asks you, one at a time. On a **Stop**, a note at the bottom right names the VMs it stops and counts the apps while they are checked (“Stopping vm-1: checking 3 apps for unsaved work… (1 of 3)”), then says when they are stopped (“vm-1 stopped”), or why not (“vm-1 was not stopped: its apps stay open.”). A VM that is installing an app says it finishes that install first (at most 60 seconds). A **Restart** says the same in its own words (“Restarting vm-1…”, then “vm-1 restarted”). Quitting shows the count alone (“Checking 3 apps for unsaved work… (1 of 3)”). An app that marks unsaved work in its window title (a `*` before its name, as GIMP and Inkscape do) asks at once. An app whose window stays open without asking anything is asked about after up to 15 seconds: it did not close when Wazza OS asked it to. An app whose window has gone but which is still quitting gets up to 30 seconds to finish, and nothing is asked when it does; if it is still running then, Wazza OS says it is still closing: **Stop now** (or **Quit now**) ends it, **Keep open** cancels and it goes on closing by itself. While another app is asking, Wazza OS does not wait for those: it asks about them after that question, and only about the ones still running. **Save** or **Keep open** on any of them cancels the Stop or the quit (after Save, the tab's Chat saves the work and you stop or quit again), and the apps that had already closed open again at once. With **Always save** or **Always close without saving** chosen ([Settings › General › Unsaved work](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#unsaved-work)), no question comes where that choice can answer: each tab's Chat saves first, or the apps close without saving, and the Stop or the quit goes on. With Always save, Wazza OS still asks about an app it could not save or could not check (and Keep open there cancels); with Always close without saving, nothing is asked. The same happens before an update that restarts Wazza OS ([Update](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/update.html)). If the window cannot answer when you quit (it is busy or reloading), a small Wazza OS dialog asks instead, "Some apps may have unsaved work. Quit anyway?": **Quit** quits, **Cancel** keeps everything open. Wazza OS never quits by itself while it cannot ask you.

When you log out or shut down the computer, Wazza OS cannot ask you: within a few seconds it notes each tab's project and asks every app to close, as your desktop does, then stops its VMs. The tabs stay and reopen at the next start. An app with unsaved work shows its own question, which the computer may not wait for: save before you log out.

### Many tabs

When the strip is full, tabs shrink to their icons, then fold into one square that shows how many there are: click the square to see every tab and pick one. How many tabs show before they fold: [General › Tabs shown before they fold](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-general.html#tabs-and-layout).

## The Desktop menu

![The Desktop menu: View: Fold Chat, Fold Desktop; Desktop: Lock input, Pop out, Full screen; FPS](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-desktop-menu.webp)

The button at the top right, left of the window buttons, on an app tab:

| Item | What it does |
|---|---|
| Fold Chat / Show Chat | Hides this tab's Chat to give the app the whole width (and back). |
| Fold Desktop / Show Desktop | Hides the app to give the Chat the whole width (and back). |
| Lock input / Unlock input | Locked, your clicks and keys no longer reach the app: watch an agent work without getting in its way. |
| Pop out | Shows the app in its own window, which you can move to another screen. Closing that window puts it back in its tab. |
| Full screen | The app fills the screen (a square at its top right opens this menu again, to leave full screen). |
| FPS | Shows the live frame rate of the app's picture, at the corner of the app. |

## The Explorer

![The Explorer panel: VM 1, Home, New file, New folder, Paste here, view buttons, and the list of the VM's home folder with names, dates, types and sizes](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/window-explorer.webp)

The button at the far left of the tab strip opens the Explorer over the Chat: the files of the VM (its home folder), with **New file**, **New folder**, **Paste here**, the views (list, grid, pictures, details), reload and close. Pick another running VM at the top. Double-click a file to open it in its app, in a new tab. More in [Files and sharing › The Explorer](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html#the-explorer).

## History

![The History page: search tabs and chats; All, Chats, Tabs, Favourites; 0 favourites, 0 recent tabs; No workstation history yet](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/history-page.webp)

History before any tab was closed.

Every tab and Chat you had, by day, with its time. Filter with **All**, **Chats**, **Tabs** or **Favourites**, or type in **Search tabs and chats** (it searches names, VMs, apps and the lines of Chats). On each entry: its star (favourite), **Open** (reopens the tab, with its Chat), and **×** (deletes the entry).

A tab you reopen from History comes back on the project it had when you closed it: its app opens the file its last save wrote (a photo GIMP saved over, or the new `.xcf` it saved beside it), and its Chat is there with the whole conversation. A favourite made from a tab reopens it the same way, on that tab's last project; any other favourite opens as it was made. When that file is no longer there, the tab says so and its app opens without it.

A [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html) session is there too, named Computer Control and without a star (it cannot be a favourite). Its **Open** shows its tab if it is open; a closed one comes back with its conversation in the VM shown, but it cannot take new messages yet: to go on, start a new Computer Control session. An entry from another VM says to show that VM first.

## Notifications

![The Notifications page: Mark all read, Clear; filters All 10, Needs you 0, Updates 0, Agents 9; notifications of package installs completed, the VM processors notice, Sandbox guest is ready](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/notifications-page.webp)

Notifications after the first start: the default packages installed, the VM ready.

Everything Wazza OS told you, newest first, each with its time and the VM and tab it concerns. Short notices also appear for a few seconds at the bottom right of the window. Filters: **All**, **Needs you** (something waits for your answer), **Updates**, **Agents**. **Mark all read** clears the count on the Home menu. A notification with an action (for example **Open owning tab**) does it in one click.

## Feedback

![The Feedback page: Tell us what went wrong, a text box, Attach image, Send feedback](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/feedback-page.webp)

Tell the Wazza team what went wrong: what happened and what you expected. You may add one image (PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 5 MB): drop it on the box, paste it, or **Attach image**. Click **Send feedback**. It is sent without your account; Wazza OS adds only its version.


---

Page: What's new in 0.3.1 (Start here)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/whats-new.html

# What's new

What changed in Wazza OS 0.3.1, since version 0.3: a lighter download with a smaller VM image that keeps your files from 0.3, Wazza OS shown as one process, one Applications page that fills your screen for every VM, and many fixes to Chats, apps, tabs and updates. Below it, what changed in 0.3 since version 0.2.0.

## 0.3.1 in short

- The Wazza OS window resizes from every edge and corner, and the cursor shows where you can drag.
- The Applications page fills the whole window, centered, and has a right-click menu everywhere: on every app, on Computer Control's tile and on the empty space (Edit layout, Add app, the other view).
- One Applications page for all your VMs, with each running VM's own CPU and memory on it and in Settings. With two or more VMs, every tab shows which VM it belongs to, an app's Edit tab too, and an Add VM or a Start that an app install holds back says so in its own words.
- A folded tab group still shows its main Chat's tab.
- Wazza OS shows as one process, wazza-os, in your system monitor, instead of separate QEMU and WebKit processes.
- The VM image is smaller (its unused files removed, then compressed), so the download is lighter. When you update from 0.3, your files, Chats and settings in the VM come over to the new image, with every file in Hermes's memories, Hermes's persona (SOUL.md), your Chrome profile and the settings of every app you added yourself, and the update checks that each of your files arrived. Your shell history, and the app settings the new image already has, start at the new defaults. Apps you installed in 0.3 download their files once more the first time you open them after the update. If that copy cannot finish at once, your Chats still start, and the copy tries again at the VM's next start. Another VM starting at the same moment no longer sends the copy to the next start.
- Settings › Disks shows the older VM images Wazza OS still keeps after an update, the room they take and what keeps them. An update removes an old image only once no VM, backup or account on this computer needs it.
- Kdenlive is no longer inside the download: it downloads the first time you open it.
- All the 3D apps install, and every app install shows its download moving, as Wazza OS's own installer now does.
- Installing an app such as Brave no longer adds a second app without an icon to Your apps, and Uninstall removes the app's package and only its own files.
- Settings › General › Web browser: one choice of browser for every web app and every web link. A link opened inside a VM goes to that browser too, the one already running in your tab, instead of starting a second copy of it, and a web app such as YouTube runs in Brave when Brave is your choice, and one that falls back to Chromium when your chosen browser cannot run it opens with its sound, instead of an "AudioDenied" error; the first web app you open in Brave on a VM where Brave never ran starts in Brave too, with no first-run analytics notice on top of it.
- Web apps and Incognito tabs keep their temporary browser profiles on the VM's disk and remove them when their tab closes, so many open web apps no longer fill the VM's memory; the private sign-in tab keeps its profile in memory only.
- wsurf installs in the snap Chromium as in every other Chromium-based browser, and websites no longer take Chromium for a bot.
- The Chat shown when Wazza OS opens starts its agent at once, so its model menu is ready, also the first time after an update. While a VM installs its security updates before its desktop, its start page says so. When the VM's disk is slow at that moment, the Chat waits for the VM and starts once it answers, instead of staying stuck. While a new Chat starts, its status shows each step of the start, such as Starting Hermes, and the slow disk while it waits for it, instead of "Chat ACP connection has not been observed" through the whole start.
- Agents look for Wazza OS's own skill for a task first, and make a file you ask for in its app's window, installing the app first when needed.
- In a Chat, a line from Wazza OS that comes while an answer is being written is shown after the answer. A folded Thinking stays folded while it runs and says it is still running. An agent's own Chat shows the same agents control as the main Chat.
- A Hermes Chat on Wazza OS MiMo sees Drive's screen, and a Chat whose model cannot read images gets a description of the screen instead.
- A subagent started from a Hermes Chat no longer shows an "ack" error.

## 0.3.1, every change by area

### Chats

- A new Chat after you sign in to Wazza OS starts on your default model.
- A "provider refused this turn" label clears when the next turn works.
- Every tool row names its tool, and a finished tool's row no longer says "Running".
- A task given to an app tab runs on the model you chose for it.
- Hermes in a VM uses the model you set for new Chats.
- A new Chat opens even while another Chat's agent is busy.
- Talking to a Chat no longer draws another Chat into its agents' group.

### Sign in and the first start

- The first start offers its private sign-in tab again.
- While the Wazza sign-in waits, Wazza OS no longer retries it again and again.
- Wazza OS's built-in model connection starts in every install, and a model provider you remove disappears from the model menu at once, with no turn sent to it.

### Updates

- When you update from 0.3 with Install now, every VM that runs while the update installs starts again with its apps, including a VM you made with Open in a new VM, at its own size, and no "Sandbox owner readiness" error is shown.
- A VM whose memory you set under the 1.25 GB a VM needs says so in its own row, and how to raise it, instead of "not enough memory".

### Apps

- Sticky Notes opens again.
- Wave Terminal, ONLYOFFICE and FreeCAD no longer cover your work with their first-run screens.
- Slides an agent makes in ONLYOFFICE show on screen.
- An app tab restored after an app update is no longer blank.
- An install that waits for the VM's own updates says so.
- Open in a new VM says on the app's card what it waits for, with Cancel, and a refusal stays there until your next action on that card.
- A new VM whose first start is refused (for example while an app installs in another VM) is removed again instead of staying in Settings › VMs, stopped, and its message no longer tells you to start it again.

### Tabs

- Switching tabs no longer shows a black page, and a switch that fails no longer freezes the window: the next switch and new Chats work without a restart.
- A web link opens in the browser tab you already have.
- An app tab always shows its own app: while the app starts, the tab says "Starting" with the app's name until the app's own window is there.
- A browser tab restored after a restart no longer opens its page again on top of the browser's own restored pages, and none of your pages is lost.
- Browser tabs keep all your sign-ins, and each browser profile keeps its own add-ons.
- A browser tab that hands its page to your running browser, or whose page the browser's own restore already shows, no longer shows as failed: it says in which tab the page opened, and that tab comes to the front.
- A task an agent gives to an app whose tab is still opening goes to that tab once it is ready, never to a second tab, and never to an idle tab whose Chat runs another agent.

### Agents

- An agent asked to stop the VMs says when they are really stopped.
- An agent's screen capture works as soon as it can see the screen.
- Hermes and its skills are set up in a new VM without waiting on other work.
- A task that has already ended is no longer started again after a late start failure.
- A Chat's agent does its web work in the apps you see, never in a hidden browser of its own.
- An agent that checks on an app it started with a wrong id is told its own app starts by their exact ids, so it can go on.
- An agent typing in a web page can press any printable key, such as "." or "@".
- A helper agent that a Chat's model asks for starts also when the request does not say whether the helper is shown, and in a Hermes Chat also when the model writes the request slightly wrong (a stray closing bracket, or true or false in quotes).

### Drive

- Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Prime read Drive's screen the same way as Hermes, and Claude Code's model gets every word of Wazza OS's answers too.

### Stability

- Wazza OS no longer closes right after you save Settings, and a Save made while another one is still writing waits for it instead of failing.
- Settings can always be saved: they are no longer refused after a few hundred saves (also after a restart), and a Chat's Settings calls are no longer refused after a long session.
- A fresh VM's kernel update no longer holds up your first app.

## What changed in 0.3, since 0.2.0

Version 0.3 (build 485dbf2b8dbf) brought these changes since version 0.2.0 (build b8069fa40737).

## In short

- Hermes, the agent inside every VM, is now version 0.23.1, and it can also run on this computer for a Local Chat, on your own Custom API.
- When a model provider refuses a turn (a wrong key, too many requests, a blocked message, a proxy refusing the connection), the Chat says what happened and what to do next, never "Internal error".
- Keys stay private: Wazza OS never shows a key back to you or to a model, whole or in part, even when a provider repeats it in an error, and no AI provider is asked anything before you give it a key or sign in.
- The model window offers Apply to: This chat, All chats, or Default for new chats, names every model in plain words, and says a Custom API model is saved in Sign In › Custom API.
- "Keep going until done", a new switch in each Chat's settings, makes your message the Chat's goal: its agent keeps working until it is done, on every agent.
- Your conversation stays with the Chat when you switch agents, reopen it from History or restart Wazza OS, now also for Hermes in a VM.
- Codex runs a new, lighter build that starts faster and uses less memory; Claude Code and Prime Agent are on newer versions.
- The skills you save in Settings now reach every Chat, whichever agent it runs.
- Chats read better: tool rows show each tool's own result, inline code and file previews are drawn cleanly, models are named in plain words, and a new Chat says it is starting.
- Regenerate and an edited message start from the conversation before the answer they replace, and a message waiting for its agent is sent once, never twice.
- Settings: you can remove a skill you added, sections with their own Save button say "Saved", and Sign In's Website switch works again.
- Copy and paste with VMs: only your own paste copies files from this computer into a VM; an app that asks for them without a paste gets nothing, and when Wazza OS cannot tell, it asks you first.
- The Apps page now works like an iPad: pages of apps you swipe through, apps you press and hold to move, and you choose how many apps fit on a page.
- Big apps such as Blender are no longer inside the download; each one downloads from its official site the first time you ask for it, so Wazza OS itself is much lighter.
- Every app now updates through Wazza OS's own update. An app you have open keeps working while its update waits, and a failed update never breaks the version you had.
- Every VM gets Ubuntu's newest kernel and its security updates, safely. A new kernel is kept only if the VM still starts and still uses your graphics card. Otherwise it goes back by itself.
- New app: Notion. Many apps were updated to newer versions.
- The browser is called Chrome when your VM runs Google Chrome, everywhere you read its name.
- Installs say what really happened in plain words, and an app can now be repaired in place from its menu.
- One tab strip for all your VMs, with each VM's CPU and RAM stacked in the Applications sidebar when several run.
- Wazza OS asks before your work is lost (Save, Close without saving, Keep open, with Save through the tab's Chat and "Remember my choice"). It asks before closing a tab, Quit, a VM's Stop or a VM's Restart, in every window, and also for the apps you started or installed yourself in a VM.
- When an app asks about its own unsaved work, its own dialog is the one question you see, and the tab stays.
- Tabs and their projects come back after a restart; History reopens the file you saved.
- Typing into a busy VM no longer drops or reorders keys. Files copied on your computer paste into VM apps.
- Wazza OS reacts to changes instead of checking over and over, so it uses less of your computer at rest.
- Some updates now install without restarting Wazza OS, wait for your apps instead of breaking them, and put the previous version back if anything fails.
- Updates explain themselves: what blocks an install, what Check now found, and which apps did not come back after a restart.
- Updates follow your proxy and install on openSUSE Tumbleweed with SELinux.
- Agents can save their own commands, several tool calls in one, and use them in every Chat, also from Hermes in a VM.
- A new Deep dark theme: pure black and neutral greys, in Wazza OS and in its Chat.
- Hundreds of smaller fixes across the tabs, the VMs, the picture of each VM, the agents and their tools, each listed below in its area.
- The tests, the guide, the build tools and Wazza OS's inner workings changed a great deal too: every such change has its own line in the sections at the end.

## Hermes (the agent in each VM, and on this computer)

- Hermes is now version 0.23.1; the GitHub Copilot sign-in it ships finds your login every time.
- A Local Chat can run Hermes on this computer, on your Custom APIs; its own connection to Wazza OS never goes through your proxy.
- A Local Chat with nothing to run on says so plainly, with a working API keys button; it also says that a Wazza sign-in alone does not run Hermes on this computer.
- When a Chat asks Hermes on this computer for a model your sign-in's plan does not offer, it says so before it starts, naming the model you asked for.
- A Hermes Chat in a VM reopens its own conversation after Wazza OS or the VM restarts, or says it could not instead of quietly starting a new one; a Chat that keeps its own conversation never takes over a half-started one meant for another Chat.
- When Hermes's model provider fails, the turn ends once, in Wazza OS's words: the same message no longer appears twice, and a failed run is never taken for an answer.
- A new Hermes Chat with nothing to run on says so in its own words instead of offering a model list that would never come; Settings, the model window and the default check offer a new Hermes Chat the same models.
- Hermes in a VM never asks its own data-sharing question: Wazza OS answers it the way you chose.
- Each of Hermes's goal notices is a paragraph of its own, never run together with the answer.
- Hermes's skills arrive at most once per Chat, so its later messages never wait for them.
- After you add your first global MCP server, a VM Chat's Hermes restarts before its next message so it can use it, and a Hermes still running background helpers is never restarted, so their results are not lost.
- Installing a global MCP server, and a long call of one of its tools, no longer end with "exit 1: no answer" while the server's work is still going on.
- The kept-elsewhere wait lives in the one bind, so no bind path can skip it.
- A VM Hermes Chat's restart for a global server's first add is decided by what its process holds, as its launcher says it at the session's start.
- The local door's timed-out call is a Local Chat's Hermes's.
- Seat "tui" is not a shell; the tab's Hermes screen is seat "hermes".
- Only a WHOLE list says "not offered"; the set mirrors the picker exactly; every parse before any write.
- The default for new Chats is chosen only from the agent's offered list, the picker's own, and takes its route from it.
- The VM addon's comment names the true place too.
- The new Chats' hint names Settings' own place, from one source.
- A refused turn is said as the provider's refusal, per status, to the person.
- Ui.do's visible Hermes check takes the tab Chat's pick its trigger carries.
- The time-limit words name their real place in Settings.
- A person-facing 'Run a visible Hermes check' in the bound tab's Desktop menu, on the tab Chat's model.
- A visible Hermes check runs on the model chosen in its tab's Chat.
- A visible Hermes run that fails after it starts closes its own terminal and its run folder.
- The visible Hermes turn runs on the person's own provider plan, chosen before anything is opened, and Wazza OS judges its receipt against that plan.
- A message whose tab is already closed is dropped once, said, never deferred for a session that cannot come.
- A background VM's tab close runs over that VM's own serial.
- The sign-in catalog snapshots the registry the payload's Hermes holds, shipped plugins included.
- A Local Hermes sandbox's own network forwards Wazza OS's local door while it is bound, keyed on the start's own door key, so a Chat's turns reach the door after a Wazza sign-in.
- When Wazza OS cancels a turn for its budget, it ends only that Chat's turn: no background work is stopped and no dead prompt waits ahead of your next message.
- After a budget cancel the Chat's goal stays active, and a failure without an HTTP status names its kind.
- The Hermes adapter of Wazza OS's ONE per-turn upstream budget: the launcher tells each failed model call, Wazza OS decides and cancels.
- A Local Chat's Hermes starts without the extra scans.
- A Local Chat's Hermes starts by Wazza OS's launcher.
- A Hermes Chat in a VM gets that VM's global MCP servers as one more server, only while the VM's list has one.
- Native's none says words true however it was reached, never "nothing is signed in yet".
- The real transition takes back Wazza OS's OpenRouter declarations.
- The Hermes sign-out of the last Anthropic account no longer raises ImportError.
- A Chat turn whose skills preload raises is never reported 'current'.
- A VM Hermes Chat makes, lists and runs the user's saved commands like a host Chat.
- Each Hermes run keeps its own view of the skills that come with Wazza OS.
- A per-turn snapshot of Wazza OS's shipped skills from the VM store.

## Claude Code

- Claude Code is on a newer version, and its start always finds the Node.js it needs.
- Claude Code on Wazza OS's sign-in runs its model in the model's real context window; the Chat's info shows that window and the point where it compacts.
- A Claude Code compaction that failed says why, and what to do when it answered nothing.
- On Wazza OS's sign-in, Claude Code's model picker lists each model once, a start on a model the sign-in does not serve says the model it really started on, and the small helper model's slot is named.
- The model button shows a model Claude Code confirmed by its settings as confirmed at once, instead of staying on pending.
- "Authentication required" on Wazza OS's sign-in now says which key was refused.
- Every Claude Code Chat checks your sign-in quickly from its own copy, and a sign-out or a sign-in is noticed at the very next check.
- Claude Code on Wazza OS's sign-in or on OpenRouter sends Anthropic nothing of its own in the background.
- A Chat's agent that has not listed its models offers what its start takes.
- Claude-agent-acp's initialize and relist contracts and the relist table re-proved at 0.106.0.
- Redact takes a name as the trailing ASCII run.
- Each Claude Code Chat gets its own auth-status cache folder in the runtime folder, writable in its sandbox in every mode.
- A Claude Code Chat on Haiku switches models again: Claude Code's report of the model it runs by its role's name is the model Wazza OS set that role on.
- The cache hit is cached of ALL the input, never over 100 %: Claude Code's input is counted with its cached part.
- Prime Agent is usable on Wazza OS's sign-in through the provider gateway, as Codex and Claude Code are.

## Codex

- Codex runs a new, lighter build: it starts faster, uses less memory, starts its program directly, reopens an earlier conversation with its tools, never hands a model its own extra agents' tools, and no longer retries a dead connection forever.
- A Codex Chat's MCP tool call is ended by the tool time limit you set in Settings, and its other calls by the command time limit.
- A Codex start that follows a switch runs the model the Chat carries, with that model's own limits and thinking level.
