- Codex on your own settings starts and names a setting its version refuses, and a sandboxed Codex asks for approvals in a way the new version accepts.
- A Codex turn on an NVIDIA model no longer fails because Wazza OS sent NVIDIA's API a thinking setting it refuses.
- When Codex's key is refused, the Chat says so in Wazza OS's words, never "Internal error".
- The listed one-line examples in Rust strings a model or the user reads (refusals, a next text, capability descriptions) are written with their top-level fields in Codex's order.
- The one-line examples a model reads in the shipped skills, the host tools and the VM twin's descriptions are written with their top-level fields in Codex's order.
- A refusal's placeholder copied back as a value is refused by its field's name, nothing run.
- Every operation's signature, every field refusal's call to make and every call handed over is written in the order Codex shows a model (its fields sorted); a saved command's name held inside an object field is said too.

## Prime Agent

- Prime Agent runs Wazza OS's own build of version 0.10.1, and your first message is no longer sent twice.
- Prime's Python cells are shown as Python cells under their own names, never as "Bash" commands.
- A Python cell that imports a module named mcp can still use Wazza OS's tools.
- When Prime drops the first part of an answer, Wazza OS puts it back from Prime's own record, after any failover note of its own.
- A Chat's model read through the gateway's ids; Prime gets its own spelling.

## Antigravity

- Antigravity's tool rows show what each tool was asked to do, from Wazza OS's own record of the call, instead of empty brackets "({})"; while a call still runs, its row shows "()".
- A tool call a model wrote as text instead of calling the tool is shown as that text, never as a nameless "Error" card with no words.
- On its first message, an Antigravity Chat says it is loading its tools while it answers.
- Antigravity's refusals from a provider are said in Wazza OS's words, never as its raw error.
- Long Wazza OS tool calls from Antigravity and Prime Agent get Wazza OS's own answer before the agent's built-in time limit cuts them off.

## Every agent

- A turn its model provider refused is labeled by that refusal, with what to do next: a wrong key, too many requests, a blocked message, a missing model, or a proxy refusing the connection; never "Internal error".
- A refusal that an agent retried past and then answered no longer shows a failure under the answer, and a Chat only ever shows its own refusal, never another Chat's.
- After a provider failure with an automatic continue planned, the Chat keeps its live session and model, and its note says the status, the tries and the wait.
- A key check, a provider's refusal or an agent's error never shows a key, whole or any 8 of its characters, even when the provider puts the key in its answer.
- No AI provider is asked anything before you give it a key or sign in, and the model catalog is read only once a key or a sign-in is held.
- A key check answered by a web page (a blocked or proxied network) is read whole and said as a refused key, never as a crash.
- An unreachable OpenRouter is checked once per wait, and a proxy's refusal ends the turn in its own words instead of being retried again and again.
- A stuck Chat says why (an unknown provider, a reply cut after it started, a reply never followed), with a working way out.
- A Chat with no model says why, how to fix it, and where to choose it: Settings › Chats & agents › New Chats.
- A Chat keeps its model when you remove its key, and says the key is missing and how to add it back.
- Switching agents hands the new agent your conversation directly, up to what its model can take, with the rest pointed to; a switch that names a model runs that model.
- "Keep going until done" in each Chat's settings makes your message the goal: the agent keeps working until it is done or blocked, on every agent, within that agent's budget.
- The skills you save in Settings reach the Chats of every agent.
- A tab's close, Stop, model switch and messages reach every helper agent it started, however deep.
- Wazza OS's guidance to agents names its tools the way each agent can really call them.
- Every agent's own connection to Wazza OS skips your proxy, so a turn on Wazza OS's gateway never goes through it.

## Models, the model window and Sign In

- The model window offers Apply to: This chat, All chats or Default for new chats, and "All chats" never gives new Chats a model of their own.
- The model window names every model in words, never by an agent's own spelling of its id; Wazza OS's own models keep one order, and its rows wrap so a sign-in's reason is read whole at any size.
- While the agent you picked for a Chat installs, the model button names that agent, never another one.
- A Custom API model is named as your Custom API, never as OpenRouter, and its row says it is saved in Sign In › Custom API, not in Wazza OS's sign-in.
- A Custom API saved after a Chat started restarts that Chat's agent on it instead of being dropped, and a Custom API's "403" is said as a rejected key.
- A Custom API reasoning model gets one thinking channel per answer, never two.
- A compaction point Wazza OS sets for an agent is labeled as Wazza OS's, with its share of the window.
- On_gateway tells "never started" from "started off the gateway".
- The provider gateway's only way out is its egress filter.
- The picker says only true words: Use names only what it has, a Custom API row is the person's Custom API, plans are told apart, and the Chat's no-model words name Settings' New Chats place.
- In a small model window the footer's word takes a line of its own and is read whole.
- An unknown VM read is never a state; 3 bounded reads, then the provider ensured anyway; NOT ENSURED said when it cannot be.
- The VM's gpu-2404 provider program, wazza-gpu-provider.
- A Sign In method you choose stays chosen when the page redraws; Web apps no longer go back to Logins by themselves.
- The turn's observation lists the notices said as its text, so the goal reads the model's own last words.
- A web app that signs in at Google follows Google's sign-in to the country's own sign-in host, accounts.google.<country>, which the guard blocked.
- Sign in no longer flickers between its options on every open: each later open first shows what it showed last.
- The model window's Persona row puts its choices on a line of their own, so its words are no longer laid out a letter or a word per line.
- (c, d): Settings' default for new Chats lists the selected agent's models its sign-ins reach, and a provider only for a model OpenRouter serves.
- The agent and model the user picks for a Chat and keeps 30 s become the default for new Chats, while that default is not one the user saved.
- Wazza OS's seamless apply (swap, reload every window, 30 s health check, rollback) and its idle gate.

## Chat

- A text file's preview card in the Chat keeps each line whole up to the card's edge and ends above the file's name, instead of breaking words and running under the name.
- Inline code in an answer is drawn without stray backticks around it.
- Tool rows show the tool's own result text, never raw JSON, and an MCP call's row names its tool once, never "Tool" twice.
- A model with no name of its own is never listed as its raw JSON id.
- A new Chat says it is starting, instead of showing an empty dark area.
- The pinned bar at the top of a Chat pins your own message, never one another sender relayed.
- Regenerate, and re-sending an edited message, start from the conversation before the answer they replace, so the new answer never carries the old one.
- Switching a Chat's agent shows one notice, and switching again before you send a message updates that same notice.
- After you press Stop, the subagents list says none is running, never that the Chat started none.
- A message waiting for its agent is sent once, never again by a later retry, and a closed tab's waiting messages go with the tab.
- The key-rejected notice's actions are separate buttons again, no longer run together.
- A Chat names the model its agent really runs, also a Local Chat that takes the default model.
- Applying a model to "All chats" changes your open Chats only; new Chats keep the default you chose.
- A Local Chat's Hermes is never offered a Custom API it cannot run.
- After a reload, earlier answers keep their model's name, never its raw id.
- The Chat an agent's CLI names comes from the registry alone, the unscoped Chat rows included; the hand list leaves the code.
- The headless CLI asks the storage's admission once at its entry; a refusal is words and exit 2, never a panic.
- One refusal code by the error's kind at every boundary.
- AgentName keeps its words; the Use button's words alone carry the fix.
- A Chat hears the results of its hidden agents as a follow-up.
- Phase 3b+3c: a VM Chat's hidden agent's Chat action runs its launch family only, refused before its source otherwise.
- /workspace to the VM's share with no share folder here is refused in words that are never empty.
- The VM's shared-folder path is never used on this computer as it is; when that folder is missing here, the Chat says what is missing and how to fix it.
- The Chat that made a command runs it by op:"run"; studio.command's exact fields.
- Wazza OS's heap gives back the ~14 MiB it idles with: trim from 4 MiB free (was 24), once at idle and again only after a 4-MiB burst.
- A download host that answered an HTTP error status is named with its answer, never "could not be reached".
- GIMP's own exit ends its controller at once, so GIMP is reaped and our controller and bridge end with it; the exit of a GIMP closed after a Chat's save is proven within a second, never after a 10-s wait.
- A check that could not see the windows never says that nothing is open.
- The could-not-check question; a remembered choice answers the save question only.
- The low-memory start notice goes once its VM is ready, and no toast covers the Chat composer.

## Settings and Sign In

- Settings sections with their own Save button, such as Time limits, now say "Saved" after you save.
- You can remove a skill you added, or your copy of a shipped one, from Settings › Skills; Remove asks first.
- Words about your skills name where you find them: Settings › Skills & learning › Skills.
- Settings shows the default model you chose for Hermes, never an empty field.
- Sign In's Website switch (Staging or Production) works again and says under its row what it did, or why it could not.
- A sign-out says how it went, even when its page refreshes while it runs.
- `logs` builds no controller and reads no Settings, so the admission never refuses it; its own log path is asked fallibly, in words.
- Every Settings place a notification or the computer check opens is the control the person uses, drawn on its page, through one drawn check.
- Deep dark, a 4th Theme of pure black and neutral greys, in Wazza OS and in its Chat.
- A VM whose own kernel line sets swiotlb keeps its own setting.

## Copy, paste and files between this computer and a VM

- Only your own paste copies a file from this computer into a VM: an app that asks for your copied files without a paste gets nothing, and the window tells you once.
- When an app asks for your copied files right after a click Wazza OS cannot tell is a paste, it asks you once, naming the app and what would be pasted; only Allow copies them.
- A file dropped on the VM's Files lands once, with its own name, never as two copies.
- In a VM's file explorer a folder is never copied into itself: Paste here, New folder and New file go into the folder you are looking at.
- Text you only select on this computer reaches only the VM's selection, never the VM's clipboard, and each such text says which it is.
- A selection made in the VM is put on this computer's PRIMARY only, never over the person's copy. Each VM text names its selection.
- A drag out of a VM gives the WebView the release GTK's drag took, so the next strip press is seen.
- Only a Wazza OS window's own page publishes the strip; the spring's word carries ids only.
- A hello naming another boot is a new binding even with the same capabilities.
- The session gates a background VM's copy, every hello naming a boot ends the other boots' drops.
- The VM folder through the controller's runtime, each session clears its own state.
- A switch away and back re-binds the same window's custody, so the drag-out's grant mints.
- A VM's drag out let go on ANOTHER VM's pane waits for its files still being copied out, takes them only when they add up, and says why when they cannot come.
- The asked line is written after the registry lock is dropped.
- The kernel step's work folder is traversable by apt's own user (0711), so apt downloads sandboxed again.
- A drop's target is a VM; "host" is refused, never written on this computer.
- A click on the feedback's uploaded or dropped image previews it large, in the box.
- After a serve-time drop the rollback runs once, never over a generation an apply already put back.

## VMs, tabs and apps

- A tab that an update held is told when it is released, so it never stays held.
- A background tab you saw once shows again after you used another VM.
- The VM's top bar no longer shows an Activities button that opened nothing.
- The VM memory notice says the VM is kept below its memory cap, names the cap the VM card shows, and no longer offers to open an unrelated tab.
- A VM made before an update gets that update's agent files at its next start.
- When the screen session under Wazza OS is lost, it first closes its VMs in order, as when you quit.
- An MCP server that stopped working gets one notice with a Repair button.
- An OS package's job is named as its card names it, never by an id.

## The Apps page

- Pages view: the Apps page shows your apps on pages like an iPad, installed apps first. Swipe or press the dots at the bottom to change pages.
- Move apps: press and hold an app for about one second, then drag it to a new place. This works in both Pages and Sections, and the other apps move out of the way as you drag.
- Settings now lets you choose how many apps fit on one page (Apps per page).
- The Apps page opens in Pages. If you chose Sections, it stays in Sections.
- App names are never cut off. A long name wraps onto two lines, even at the smallest size.
- Web apps are named "<Name> Web App" (for example "Gmail Web App"), and each one keeps its own folder for the files it saves.
- Apps no longer change places while you are looking at the Apps page.
- A menu you open on an app keeps working when the page refreshes during an install, so your click is never lost.
- A card you press while installs refresh the page still opens.
- An app's own start page no longer shows the "Sections | Pages" switch that belongs to the Apps page.
- The number of apps no longer jumps while Wazza OS checks which apps are installed.
- Every time you open the Apps page, it checks each app again in the VM, so an app with an update waiting says "Update and open" right away instead of "Installed".
- The Apps page now shows all your saved apps, up to 256, instead of stopping at 64.
- The Apps page's compact controls are drawn at their own sizes again (small page dots, the "Sections | Pages" labels whole and centred in their pill).

## Getting, repairing and removing apps

- Big apps such as Blender are no longer packed inside Wazza OS. Each one downloads from its official site when you first ask for it, and all its tools for your agents still work.
- While one of those apps downloads, its card says what it is downloading.
- New app: Notion (Notion's own desktop app, from Notion's own repository).
- Notion's card tells you when Notion's repository no longer offers the version this release was tested with.
- An app you install yourself with apt inside a VM now appears in your Apps like any other app, with its own card.
- Repair: an installed app's menu now offers Repair. It installs the app again over itself, keeps your files, and never runs while the app is open.
- If a system repair inside the VM removed something an app needs, that app's own install brings it back the next time the VM starts. Anything it cannot bring back is said once, with what you can do.
- Removing Wave Terminal now removes every file its install placed.
- Removing an app that had replaced a program of the VM's own puts that program's entry back.
- An installer now says the true state of its own run, never "already installed" right after it installed the app.
- A failed install says the package system's own reason in full, instead of a vague network error.
- An install an agent starts in the background stays in the background; it no longer brings an app to the front.
- An app you added yourself can change "Opens a file" in Edit app, and after an Apply that changed its install, its card offers the update.
- An added app that keeps a separate copy for each tab says so on its card.
- Add app can add an app's MCP part as a global MCP server, so every Chat of every VM can use its tools.
- Wazza OS's own product version is 0.3.0, so the packages are wazza-os_0.3.0+git..., and the notes, the changelogs and the guide say Wazza OS 0.3.
- Restage puts its handler and the mask it found back before its cleanup.
- Restage lets its own SIGTERM through whatever mask its parent left.
- The app's own package is never an extra, so it is never marked auto.
- A Remove stops the background security download first, and the download keeps nothing for a removed app; a stop waits while the VM's start-up steps are held.
- The default installs' notice words are joined strings, never template literals.
- A package in a trigger state is a done state, so a person's app waiting for a trigger is never removed.
- The DEBUG log carries a job step's own output, its secrets scrubbed; a release logs none.
- Every start puts the VM's helper files back from Wazza OS's own copy, without the agent.
- Package installs in the VM are no longer slowed by a hook that is not needed.
- The command wazza-os --uninstall is handled first, before anything else starts.
- The kernel job's own apt-mark calls keep apt's cache in memory.
- The desktop provisioning's apt calls keep apt's cache in memory, and the bootstrap's disk hygiene never removes apt's caches.
- Apt's Post-Invoke hook starts the Python shim ONLY when a wrapped tool was replaced.
- Apt's hook never fails apt even before the shim runs; the done mark's scope said; two kills by assertion.
- The runtime bootstrap restarts the VM's helper only when a file it runs or holds loaded changed, so a re-attach that reinstalls the same software never ends the VM's Chats.
- An open that joined an install whose first view has closed is carried on by that install: the app opens after the install's own check of the VM, and nothing is done twice.
- A boot pass that could not make an app's view is recorded, and the app reads INCOMPLETE, never "not installed".
- A routed package manager keeps the caller's working directory; the places lock on its own file.
- A folder an install may remove and make again is held at its PARENT; LOST is a detector only.
- Side-by-side app versions in the VM (wazza-app-versions) and the uninstall that removes them.

## Updates for apps

- Every built-in app, older ones included, now updates through Wazza OS's own update. When an app's update is ready, its card says so.
- An app you already have open keeps working while its update waits. The new version installs the next time you open the app ("Update ready: it installs at the next open").
- Each version of an app installs into its own folder, so an update never replaces what an open tab is running.
- If an update fails, the version you had stays whole and still opens.
- "Update and open" appears only for apps Wazza OS installed. If an install replaces a program Wazza OS did not install, the card says so before you click.
- Newer versions: VSCodium 1.143, Zed 1.28.1, GIMP 3.2.8, Discord 1.0.168, Telegram Desktop 7.4.3, Postiz 2.25.3, Node.js 24.22.3 (for Wazza OS and the five apps that use it), Playwright 1.65 with its Chromium 158, Remotion 4.0.543 (Motion Studio), yt-dlp 2026.10.26 (Video Toolkit), and the FreeCAD tools.
- The three single-link checks that guard package-directory files take a live update hold's own second link, proved by ONE shared module.
- A private apt update or download no longer holds every app install behind the apt lock.
- Apt's own update no longer fails inside an install job.
- Every wait of one Update now reads that Update now's ONE wait id, so an install started after the click never holds it; the hold path keeps the one bound itself and never retries hot.
- A Chat's turn that holds the seamless apply's refresh sends it back to its wait under ONE bound for the whole Update now; no recursion.
- A Wazza folder that failed to mount when the VM became ready is tried once more during that start.
- A card's read never waits for a saved app's update check.
- The seamless update wired end to end (overlay <- client, apply backend <- overlay).
- The UI overlay of Wazza OS's seamless update (verified generation served at the same origin, embedded fallback).

## The VM's system and its first installs

- Every VM now gets Ubuntu 24.04's newest kernel and its security updates.
- A new kernel is kept only if the VM still starts and still renders on your computer's graphics card. If not, the VM goes back to its previous kernel by itself.
- The security updates install at the VM's next start, before its desktop, so they never interrupt your apps.
- The VM kernel updates row on the Apps page says the same thing as its card.
- Security downloads run in the background after the VM's first installs. A slow or unreachable download address is retried on another address, then on your country's mirror.
- A first-start install that fails is tried once per VM start, then once a day, instead of over and over.
- A first-start install no longer stays "uncertain"; it ends installed, or says why not.
- Places & routes (OSM) installs even on a slow network: its optional online check can no longer make the install fail.

## Browsers

- The browser app is called "Chrome" when your VM runs Google Chrome and "Chromium" otherwise, on its card, its tab and everywhere else you read its name.
- Google Chrome installs again: its repository's signing key is accepted.
- The wsurf add-on now comes installed in the Chromium-family browsers Wazza OS installs: Chromium, Brave and Opera.
- When Chrome cannot start, its error page now names the real cause instead of an unrelated line.
- Chrome's per-tab profiles get a root of their own; a Chrome tab whose Chrome is gone is refused.
- A hint's removal reads only the shown hint's element.
- A hint dies with its element, so a tab closed under the pointer leaves no tooltip behind.
- The GPU provider delivered to each VM, re-run when its last Chromium tab closes.
- Settings > Skills & learning names each app as the shown VM shows it.
- Settings > General > Unsaved work names no browser.
- Chrome's background install runs its script as written.
- The browser app's removal purges the Google Chrome that Wazza OS installed.
- The index checks ids, not signatures; an add-on ships only when its licence allows.
- Settings_auth's chrome actions wait for the runtime bounded, queued once, never answered busy at 25 ms.
- The strict-field refusal names EVERY field the operation does not take in one refusal, inside the operation or beside it.
- The per-tab seed copies config files only, never the person's logins or browser storage, and never a leveldb or SQLite file.

## Apps, one by one

- Blender, GIMP, Kdenlive and Inkscape: when an agent saves your work, it saves through the app's own Save and checks the file before saying it is saved.
- VSCodium: unsaved work from a closed VSCodium tab comes back in your next VSCodium tab.
- FreeCAD: shape creation now uses every size and setting you give it.
- FreeCAD answers right away while it starts, instead of looking frozen.
- Kdenlive installs its platform parts from Wazza OS's own copy, so it installs without the internet.
- Postiz: opening a Postiz tab no longer ends its own session, and its first start no longer leaves an extra process behind.

## The tab strip

- One tab strip for all your VMs: a tab of another VM is just a tab, and pressing it shows that VM and that tab.
- When several VMs run, each VM's CPU and RAM are stacked at the bottom left of the Applications sidebar.
- Showing another VM keeps the tabs of the VM you were on in the strip.
- A press on another VM's tab looks selected at once, and the VM shown changes as soon as the switch is done.
- A press on another VM's Chat or Applications tab now opens it.
- The x on another VM's tab closes its app in that VM without moving your view; with unsaved work you are asked there, and the question names the VM.
- Closing a tab while Wazza OS is still showing its VM is no longer lost.
- During a switch to another VM the picture says a switch is running, and what you type for the VM you are leaving is not sent to the wrong VM.
- Tabs share the strip's width evenly.
- Tab groups start folded, and nothing of a group is drawn taller than the strip.
- A VM's tab with no app reads "Desktop", not a number.
- The x on each tab is drawn cleanly, and a click right on the cross of the Settings or History tab closes it.
- Enter or Space on a focused tab switches to it.
- Closing another tab no longer takes the Settings tab with it.
- A tab with no desktop, such as a VM's Chat tab, gets a hover card too.
- A hover card no longer shows an old picture after a switch, and a busy VM's hover card says it is busy.
- Hold a dragged file over a tab to switch to it, drop it on another VM's tab to copy it into that VM's Downloads, and a drop during a switch goes to the new tab.
- A click on the Applications sidebar's own empty space folds the sidebar.
- Each helper a Chat starts, such as Computer Control, gets its own visible tab.
- A start or close that can never finish no longer shows "Starting…" or "Closing…" forever, and a window that never comes or a failed start is said in plain words.
- An agent's CLI acts only on its own tab's Chat or its own VM, reads included, by the registry's own scope.
- A tab's could-not-check question is withdrawn once that tab is gone, never left drawn over another tab.
- The Installing page's phase chips read 'Starting · Running', never 'Running · Starting · Running'.
- An OS package installs in the background unless the person's request has focus:true.
- A medium model window names its tabs as a small one does, so Apply to's three choices keep the header on one row.
- The Desktop menu's Run uses the model chosen in the tab's Chat.
- A hidden agent's own launch is checked on its ROOT tab's app.
- The holds files are read with the plain one-link rule, never through the hold-link proof (no recursion).
- Wazza OS's own window requests are marked as its own, and Escape in the activities overview never reaches an app.
- Cleanup: the strip's over-limit plumbing that drew nothing differently is removed.
- A default install busy on an unread VM is decided again on the event that ends it.
- No app's tab open, no simulation; every shadowed tool lifted for the install and bound back.
- The one strip makes nothing per drawing when nothing changed, and nothing for one VM.
- A record-gone line counts as "nothing was sent" only when it names THIS close's own record.
- The flock locks in /run/wazza-tabs are opened read-only, so taking one wakes no app supervisor.
- A certain stop forgets the tab selected in its boot, so a new boot's tabs open.
- A custom app's supervisor, the tab group's leader, stays while its session holds its app, so the receipt stays live and exact for the app's whole life.
- A forking launcher's window is proven: the group read survives dash's errexit.
- A person's show that the navigation's preflight refuses writes its WZTX failed line.
- A background start's record goes with its VM boot; the chip shows the app after Stop + Start.
- An app start that hands its window to a copy already running ends at once with words that say so, instead of starting again on its own.
- A VM's Restart through main's windows' coordinator asks its private question, its app rows and its could-not-check and silent-window questions in the Restart's words, not as a Stop.
- A second copy of an app started in its own session still reaches the desktop's accessibility service, so a screen reader sees its window.
- Two tabs of one single-copy app started at almost the same moment never leave an extra empty "Untitled Document" in the other tab's window.
- A start whose launcher returned while the app it started still runs is waited for like any start, never taken for an ended start or a hand-off.
- A single-instance app whose start handed its window to a copy already running is started once more inside its own session bus, so it opens in its own tab.
- A Wazza OS still starting, with no app opened yet, says so in its fail-safe question.
- An Add app app started without its file says what is true and what the person can do, never a control that does not exist.
- An app started without the file it was given says so at its FIRST open, drawn, and an "Add app" app says where its file opening is set.
- "refuse S <vm> <tab>" refuses every arm of one tab for S seconds.
- The documents read checks the same VM, Runtime and VM boot, not the close's strict tuple.
- An app on no tab's workspace starts again after a VM restart.
- An orphan app moves with its designation and starts once after a VM restart.
- A Desktop dock launch handed over to a copy outside the tab is said on the tab, never claimed on a guess.
- The documents read names the exact route it asks about.
- A folder installed before versions is held for its tabs; migrate and the first versioned activate go on.
- The profile launcher records what it did with a tab's start file.
- A tab keeps its older snapshot across INSTALLING APPS; one lock over every app's holds.
- Packages and saved apps' outside-root writes are HELD for running tabs, never waited for.
- A Chat's quiet sign a few ms early on the loop's clock still ends a save's turn.
- A file name names a tab's title only as a WHOLE name.
- An agent's force on a Desktop tab ends the apps it shows, through K's discard.
- A repair of the running version a live tab may run waits before anything is staged (rule (b)), no download loop.
- A VM with no tab is swept; capped windows ask.
- A reinstall's checked copy replaces a damaged version folder no live tab runs.
- A question that comes from another app on the tab's workspace says so.
- The stop guard's mark is the tab's; a running VM with no ready route is asked about.
- Owner-documents names each live tab's current saved project, generically.
- App_available_inner keeps its one-argument form for its callers (the strict gate).

## Closing apps without losing work (the close guard)

- Closing an app tab with unsaved work asks: Save, Close without saving, or Keep open.
- Save can go through the tab's Chat, and Wazza OS checks that the save really happened before the tab closes.
- "Remember my choice" keeps your answer across windows and restarts; a remembered close without saving is checked, and you are asked if the app did not end.
- Quit, a VM's Stop and a VM's Restart ask about unsaved work first, in every Wazza OS window.
- A Desktop tab's x asks about the apps you started inside it, and Close without saving ends them.
- Apps you installed yourself in a VM get the same questions, and they come back after a restart.
- A running VM with no tab gets its apps asked about before a Stop, a Quit or a restart.
- Keep open after a Stop starts again the apps the Stop had already closed.
- When Wazza OS cannot tell whether an app has unsaved work, it never ends it unasked.
- A Stop, a Quit or a close after Keep open is asked again, never ignored.
- Keys you were typing for something else never pick an answer in a close question.
- When an app asks about its own unsaved work, such as GIMP's own dialog, that is the only question, the tab stays, and Wazza OS offers Save with the Chat.
- A Chat's close of an app tab is no longer blocked by a window the app already had open, such as a welcome window.
- An app that is already quitting is not asked about, its tab closes when it ends, and a question on screen goes when the app's window goes.
- A close that fails after the app's window went says so, and no empty ghost tab stays.
- A Chat that tries to close a tab while you answer its close question is told you are deciding.
- A Chat can force a close only after a warning about that tab, and a forced close never ends something you are being asked about.
- A Chat closing the same tab again and again never ends an app whose close waits for your answer.
- A Desktop tab is never closed over apps that Wazza OS could not ask.
- Cancelling a start that is stuck never kills an app that is already running with your work.
- An app without a window is asked to end politely and given time before it is stopped.
- After Stop and Keep open, an app that was still closing reopens once it has ended, and a Stop waits for an app still quitting instead of asking about it.
- Save then close finishes as your own close, even if the Wazza OS window refreshes in between.
- Keep open closes the app's own dialog that the close brought up, and the keyboard goes back to your window.
- "Always save" shows what a Stop waits for, saves every app at once, and says why one could not be saved.
- The window's Stop names the VMs it stops and shows its progress in words, and a VM's Restart asks in its own words.
- An OS log-out, a shutdown or a kill of Wazza OS records each tab's project and asks about unsaved work where it can.
- If a Wazza OS window loses its screen, its questions are asked in another Wazza OS window.
- When an app ends by itself, its tab closes and Wazza OS tells you.
- When a VM shuts down from inside, its apps' tabs close, and a reboot from inside starts it again through Wazza OS's own Start.
- Private tabs (Chromium Incognito) are never ended by Restart Wazza OS for a core update, Quit and a VM's Stop ask first, and they are never recorded.
- Native's boot heal is never cancelled by the latch its own stop raises; only the app's close cancels it after that stop.
- The page going away disposes the tabs controller; the save it owes is written, then nothing is drawn or saved.
- A tab's waiting close question learns its gone window from the selection's own answer, at once.
- A background close moves the view only when its app is seen asking.
- A close whose request finds its tab's record gone was never sent: asked at once, said so.
- History's Save As read ends at the tab's close, not its last visit; an empty read says so.
- A new tab of a VS Code-family app copies only that app's own user settings, never a database file and never through a link, so your logins, data, unsaved work, history and transcripts are never copied.
- The checked end's idle check no longer counts the app group's own resident supervisor as the app's work, so a remembered "Close without saving" ends an idle SAVED app showing its prompt.
- A Desktop tab's own apps are worded open IN it, never "outside" it; its Close without saving says they close with it.
- An ended app's row never holds a live app's question.
- A start during a Quit waits for the quitting Wazza OS to end, then opens.
- An agent's Chat start survives another window closing meanwhile; an ended agent's tab answers ended.
- Close without saving ends the app in the Desktop tab's own group, and each app left running says why.
- A studio window's close asks in the page, never with window.confirm.
- A close again quits anyway only once the person was told so.
- Vm_cancel_apps_close acts only for a Wazza OS window.
- Always close without saving answers every question.
- Quit never goes on for a guard that could not check.
- A window list read that fails while windows close is read again; a Stop's sweep never dies of it.
- A Stop's question closes by itself once its app has ended; slow quits get a grace.
- A VM's Stop, Quit or restart also asks a foreign app on no tab's workspace.
- An agent's application close answers blocked with its choices when the app asks to save.
- Escape for an in-window prompt only after a close really asked.
- A Quit the window cannot answer asks the person natively, never quits by itself.
- A failing close guard keeps an engine restart, an app update or a tab's close; only Quit and Stop VM go on.
- The Stop VM close guard and its four entry points.
- Cancel an app's own "Save changes?", one close sweep per VM, and the Quit guard.
- The close guard's host commands and its one UI interface.
- Owner-close-cancel and owners-close-sweep.

## Tabs coming back: restore, History and Favourites

- Each tab's project is remembered, so a restored tab opens the same work.
- Reopening a tab from History opens the file you saved, even under a new name with Save As.
- History names each entry's app by its name.
- History and Favourites reopen a tab whose close had failed, or say why they cannot.
- History and Favourites keep each tab's own entry, and the Favourite star matches it.
- Settings > General > Tabs & layout can turn tab restore Off, said in plain words.
- A VM that ran when Wazza OS stopped comes back at the next start, and tabs of VMs not shown are restored too.
- Tabs come back even when a VM gets ready late.
- After an update of Wazza OS, the tabs that were open come back.
- Refreshing the Wazza OS window no longer breaks restored tabs.
- A restored tab whose app starts without its document says so, and a failed relaunch after a VM restart is said on the tab.
- The tab list keeps up to 8 VMs, forgets a deleted VM's tabs, and one damaged entry no longer loses the whole list.
- A background start stays its own across its restore's saved-as follow; the chip shows the app.
- A start that waited for another tab's start of a program that owns no session-bus name lets the start lock go at once, so the tabs of such an app restored together wait for the first start only, never for each other in turn.
- A person's own start of an app from the dock, the app grid or the search on a Desktop tab takes the focus; a restore still never steals it.
- A tab another package's hold marked behind is still told of its own app's update, once.
- A tab restored behind the view whose saved document its app refuses starts once more without it and says why, as the shown tab's own start does.
- A start file the desktop user cannot read is refused with why, so a restored tab's words say it, never an app failing on its own in silence.
- A Stop question's read of its app backs off, and the app's exit wakes it.
- A window lost in an earlier VM boot is no fact of the next one.
- Pressing Start again never spoils a command already on its way, and a restore opens the installed version.
- After an app updates beside a running tab, that tab's Reload reopens its project in the new version.
- A project on a host share, /mnt or /media is restored too.
- Desktop from the launcher shows the restored Desktop tab whose apps still have to start.
- After a VM restart while Wazza OS runs, every background app tab restores again.
- A run command written as a desktop Exec takes the tab's file, so Add app and agent apps restore their project.

## Tabs while apps update

- An app being updated shows "Updating" on its tab, and starting it waits for the update instead of failing.
- A tab still on the version from before an update says so, with a one-click Reopen in the new version.
- An update keeps the version that last launched until the new version has launched.
- "Update and open" is offered only when an update is ready.
- A tab's GIMP reads Wazza OS's system gimprc, shipped in the VM helper assets, so GIMP's own update check is off and its "Update available" box never comes over the image.
- A held tab's note names what the update replaced.
- A held tab's note no longer names the tab's own app; its words are true whatever the update replaced.
- A tab manifest that cannot be read blocks only an update of an installed app, logged; ffmpeg gets no guard.
- No VM refusal says the update waits for the other tabs; the rare one installs at the next open.
- A tab keeps its older snapshot, and every install records where it wrote, so the next update keeps it.
- The hold registry: a running tab keeps the old files of a system directory an update replaces.
- Every open of a plan app reads the VM and updates first; the gate takes a previous version only after a failed update.
- The chip's Updating words join the tab's name by concatenation, not a template.

## VMs

- When memory is short, a new VM's Start waits for the running VMs to give back unused memory, and says what kept it if it still cannot start.
- An app start refused for lack of memory says so at once, in words.
- A VM boot that stalls is started again once, and every window's boot page says so.
- A stopped VM's page stays stopped, and Settings > VMs updates by itself when your VMs change.
- If an app tab's keys and clicks cannot work, the tab says so in words.
- Ctrl+Alt+Space is the VM's Super key on every computer and opens that VM's Wazza OS app launcher.
- The VM card names the VM's graphics once, on one line.
- Every VM process end forgets its start record.
- The supervisor never ends itself while its app runs; a failed read is transient, another identity ends it at once, and a window's end with members left holds on, unanchored.
- The VM call's selector is checked by the registry's own VM id rule.
- The controller's build script watches vm/addons/shipped-commands only while it exists.
- An app's release of the fullscreen it took over Wazza OS's gives the window Wazza OS's fullscreen back.
- The proof module's words name its loaders and why holds files need no publish wait.
- A Start's boot stages are written only by holders of its run; quiet() goes.
- A switch to a running VM says "Switching to vm-N…", never Select and start this VM.
- One stale-route rule for an off-line run's polls and the vm-kernel confirm's tries; a failed route read is logged in debug builds.
- An off-line launch's polls renew a route that went stale after its start, for the same VM and boot.
- A secondary VM's launch receipt is its route's launch on the same VM boot.
- Ending an agent ends what it started, the deepest first, through one walk.
- An agent may start its own, within its own scope; every grant it made ends with its own.
- When a trial start of vm-1 with a new kernel ends by itself, Wazza OS knows that the VM stopped.
- Wazza OS ships its own two commands, a bash report and a tool chain.
- A stalled boot of a pending kernel trial is the trial kernel's, never vsock's.
- The build stamp watches only this worktree's own HEAD, its own reflog and its branch's loose ref file, never the common packed-refs or a refs/ directory.
- The door's snapshot is WebKit's own drawing; the runner reads it.
- The confirm's POLLS renew a stale route for the same VM and boot; only the confirm.
- The confirm renews a stale route for the same VM and the same boot only.
- The vm-kernel confirm waits out a try refused before dispatch, and a confirm never dispatched gives its boot back.
- The loopback VM never runs a VM system or session command on the host.
- One checked join from a VM share path to the host's share; an escape is refused, never rewritten.
- The QEMU launcher takes the running entrypoint named "wazza-os" too.
- A page loaded during a long network hold says the VM's notice from its launch receipt.
- The network is proved in the background as a detached VM job.
- A bootstrap of an address whose agent a bootstrap KEPT less than 60 s before restarts the agent anyway.
- Tab_private_windows is granted to the main window and the Wazza OS windows, as every app command must be.
- The idle VM compacts at 32 MiB of new scattered free memory and after its RAM changes size; r7e-archkde kept 241 MiB of free VM memory on the host with no compaction.
- The write over a person's own file keeps its extended attributes, its access list included, as it keeps its mode.
- An app whose command names no place for its file refuses an open with a file in words, never an empty start, never a guess.
- The write over a person's own file goes to a temporary file beside it and replaces it only once proven; a .xcf name taken while it is chosen moves on to the next free one.
- The desktop user's own open of a start file decides, so a readable file in a folder they cannot enter is refused too, naming that folder.
- Stop line race, the last line: a Restart whose line was superseded by a Stop says nothing more when its start fails; only a Restart with no line at all falls back to its words.
- Free memory goes back in 2 MiB blocks, the host's huge page; 4 KiB reporting was undone by khugepaged.
- Nothing on the start page or in the VM selection waits forever.
- Activate rolls back what a failed step left; a staging folder a job holds is never trashed.
- A Start that finds an Uncertain lifecycle is not memory-gated (it adopts or refuses, never launches).
- --force stays off the usage line (an agent tool's table mirrors it); a stop the window did not take names it.
- A hold never covers a folder under the user's mount places (/mnt, /media; /run already).
- The person's explicit hard stop, vm stop vm-N --force / {force: true}, stays a choice.
- A Start that skipped its memory admission never launches a new generation.
- Gc and the trash never delete a version a process still uses through a lazily detached root view.
- The low-memory notice also goes once the boot page sees the VM QEMU running.
- Vm-scope keeps the last good window list when a round's read fails.
- Every Wazza OS build cuts its seamless bundle from the UI its binary embeds.
- A plan no reload followed within 60 s never shapes a later page end (an apply that stopped).

## Keyboard, clipboard and files into VMs

- Typing while a VM is busy no longer drops keys or types them late; if some could not be typed, Wazza OS tells you how many.
- Copy files on your computer and paste them into an app in a VM; one copied picture or picture file pastes as that picture.
- Your copied files go into a VM only when you paste there.
- "Pasted" is said only for a real paste, and a paste whose files could not reach the VM says why.
- The held set cleans every key of every key ring, so a rotation's second key never reaches the Chat.
- A chat turn's error never carries a key Wazza OS sends upstream, whole or any 8 of its characters.
- Fail closed on a tail cut inside a private key block.
- The window's VM bar gets a Keys menu that sends the chords this computer's desktop would take (Ctrl+Alt+T, Alt+F4, Alt+Tab, Alt+F2, Ctrl+Alt+Delete, Print Screen) to the VM shown.
- A cross-VM switch's window is told its start and end again (no stale 'Not sent' line), and a Desktop start's input arm waits for the window's focus instead of saying it failed.
- The VM helper leaves the Activities Overview by GNOME Shell's own OverviewActive property, never by an Escape key into the focused window.
- Tabd's op focus answers the person's in-view tab, which holds no lane, from the core master keyboard.
- Tabd activates the person's in-view tab's main window once per view, so its app takes the person's keys without a click first.
- A Desktop start's input is not moved under while it arms.
- A debug-build-only fault hook that refuses the next VM input arms, to prove the arm's recovery live.
- One input-arm or surface-ack timeout no longer locks a shown tab's keys for good.
- The keyboard focus goes back after a cancel's Escape.
- A key ring's leftover mode or key names are no credential.

## Native GPU (a graphics card lent to a VM)

- Lending a graphics card always works with the VM that has the card, never with whichever VM is shown.
- A Native GPU restart restarts only the VM the card is lent to, asks first (Restart them all or Not now), and your view comes back to that VM.
- A Native GPU restart asks about unsaved work before it stops any VM.
- Native GPU's restart question comes up at once in a Wazza OS window you are not using.
- The Wazza OS command line and its MCP tools can answer Native GPU's restart question, and it stays your own answer.
- (Blender paste): a copied picture pastes into Blender: Image > Paste Image and Ctrl+V in the Image Editor, 3D View > Add > Image > Reference from Clipboard.

## The picture of each VM, and Wazza OS's own use of your computer

- A tab you leave keeps its last picture while you look at another VM, so switching back shows it at once.
- A VM's first app tab and a tab being fitted show no black bands.
- Blender's starting card stays until Blender's first picture is drawn.
- Each app window is shown in the tab it belongs to, and app tabs are kept apart from each other.
- Wazza OS no longer polls while you do nothing; it reacts when something changes, so it uses less CPU at rest.
- A Chat window open for one Chat closes when the frame shows another Chat, another session of its tab, or a tab with no Chat.
- An opened call that has not ended says Running..., and it is drawn again when it ends.
- A done helper's square leaves the strip at the end of its parent's turn; the agents panel keeps it.
- Once the host holds an off-line command's answer, its folders end at once, so a surrender's secrets never stay in the VM's .done.
- The install and background capture boundaries ask the one refusal code.
- A list item's own indented code (its content's indent plus 4, after a blank line) is kept as code.
- A raw HTML block of CommonMark's kinds 1-5 is kept to its own close, not to its first blank line.
- A 4-space line is indented code only after a blank line, at the start or in a code block, never in a list.
- The markdown hook's memo is bounded by size as well as count; its words say a streamed update is read whole.
- A Chat's markdown gets each path's '_' and '*' escaped, so the path is drawn as written and linked whole.
- The window's tool cards and thinking blocks had no caller; they go, with the rules only they drew.
- The Chat frame's look has ONE copy, the preload's #wazza-chat-look; the window writes no style into the frame and only syncs its theme.
- A VM whose GPU this computer cannot give says why in true words; with no GPU at all it runs on software graphics, otherwise its notice offers that VM's own CPU only choice.
- The no-backtick rule lives in the palette's own style, which the window never replaces, so an answer's inline code draws no backticks on the stack.
- A gateway turn whose upstream the person's proxy refused says the proxy refused.
- Native names its own Sign In by the product's name in the shared strings; the picker no longer rewrites them.
- A failed display start's cleanup takes the one stop order, so a producer still holding its ordered consumer never makes the detach refuse.
- A picture dropped on a card drawn over the feedback box no longer lands in the box.
- Product-started messages carry their true sender, Wazza OS.
- Words that name a place in Settings name the right page and label.
- A turn stopped at its time limit names the Time limits place, by its limit.
- A VM the person started CPU-only (Settings > GPU None) takes its software renderer as desktop readiness; a GPU-mode VM keeps the strict VirGL gate.
- Wazza-sync, one lock depth for the whole binary.
- A provider's refusal of a Chat turn is its one error row, and the Chat's session and model stay.
- The model button's avatar keeps its own box beside the label; only a failure's words and the label shrink.
- A failed start's words in the model button end in an ellipsis inside it, the whole words its hint.
- Antigravity and Prime Agent, the harnesses with no in-place re-open; the announce at the change.
- A hidden agent's own windowless prompt captures as a Wazza OS parent, with its own session's document.
- A Chat lists its hidden agents' own hidden agents, and its graph draws them under them.
- A follow-up message refused only for now waits, and is sent once again when its cause ends.
- Turn it on and Undo are requests applied when the person logs out, never a live write of GNOME's setting.
- A refused turn is reported only for the Chat it belongs to, never as another Chat's refusal.
- A video tile's length lies inside its square at every tile size; the Chat's media look has one copy, a preload style the window never replaces.
- Option B (2) fix: a value GNOME may have changed is never said unchanged, and a change Wazza OS cannot undo names the person's own undo.
- Option B: at a fractional display scale, Settings > This computer says how GNOME draws Wazza OS and offers GNOME's one setting that makes it sharp.
- After a Wazza sign-in, a started Hermes Chat still on its never-chosen signed-out default follows the door default, so its labels name the model that runs.
- The theme customizer: six colours over a base theme, an exact live preview, applied by its button.
- A parent Chat reads its helpers at its turn's END, and ONE writer tells both readers of its helper rows.
- The agents graph draws the whole tree; a visible agent's x stops its subtree first.
- Chat_element_read finds a control by its role and accessible name, opt-in by `name`.
- A length badge's text is light grey in dark mode, never pure white.
- The turn's way-out button carries its test id only in a DEBUG build; the debug flag is read once per page.
- The goal reads the final line of the answer's LAST message, from the turn's ordered blocks.
- Slice 1a: a fence in the answer opens and closes as CommonMark's do, so a shorter or other fence inside it never ends it.
- ONE subagent control instead of the top strip and the two icons.
- A video in a Chat is its POSTER, the VM's own ffmpeg's one frame, with its length; the viewer plays it on Play here only.
- A Chat's goal counts as done or blocked only when the answer's last line says so, and a held goal's queued turn never starts.
- -SILENT: a turn that has said nothing is watched, asked about and said in words again.
- An app whose group leader is gone is asked at the first x, in true words, and its reserved row is never torn down unasked.
- Each render takes a free playlist name, so two renders in one millisecond never collide.
- /#38: the stuck words' way out has its test id, so the live row clicks it as the person does.
- /#38: a stuck Chat's watch is this run's, never saved with the Chat (a restored Chat watches its reply afresh).
- A dropped reply's late result changes nothing.
- /#38: a stuck Chat's words carry a working way out; the resume is bounded.
- Claude Code compacts at 90% of the window it runs the Chat's model in, not at ~93k, and a compaction of its own that failed is said in one line.
- A message sent while a turn ran goes once that turn failed, instead of waiting for a next step that never comes.
- A provider's failure no longer ends a Chat for good: the gateway asks again at once, and the Chat goes on by itself later.
- Signed out with no provider, the default for new Chats has no model and no provider; a Chat binds with no model, says why and never starts.
- An agent Wazza OS installs when it is picked (Antigravity) is offered as available: "installs when picked", selectable as the default, whose save installs it.
- The default for new Chats keeps the thinking level picked with it, and a new Chat on it starts at that level.
- An app tab's x reads its own project first while another run of its app is live.
- A Wave started outside any tab never shares a profile with a Terminal tab's Wave, so the tab never hands over to it and fails.
- In a Wayland session the wait also needs the X display Wazza OS's windows use.
- The relaunch's dialog helper is dispatched (it never was), runs on the desktop's X display, and a run of the built binary proves it; DriWatch always ends its thread.
- An unsent answer is sent again, labels keep their underscores, and a login start waits for its render node.
- A Chat whose send fails before any turn still gets its wake.
- A Chat whose message is being sent sets no wake of its own.
- A tab's project outside your home folder (in /mnt, /media or /run/media) is remembered too.
- The capture rounds ask the VM only when a project may have changed.
- The page after a planned refresh keeps the running stream through its restore, so the restored tab adopts it (no picture gap).
- A refresh Wazza OS plans keeps the VM's picture: no stream stop, no surface clear, no boot page over a ready VM.

## Updating Wazza OS

- Some updates of Wazza OS now install without a restart. Home > Update says so, shows the download size, offers Update now or Later, says what it is waiting for, and puts the previous version back if anything fails.
- An update without a restart waits for your busy apps and your unsaved work instead of breaking them, and a Restart you refuse opens again what it had closed.
- The skills and instructions Wazza OS gives the agents in your VMs now come with Wazza OS itself, and every Chat in a VM uses the set your Wazza OS serves.
- When an update needs Wazza OS to restart, it first asks your open apps about unsaved work, then restarts with none open.
- An update that cannot install says why before it downloads, in plain words: for example a missing pkexec, with the command that installs it, and the update stays ready to try again.
- When there is no new version, Check now says nothing is published yet instead of "check failed", and the update server's own errors are said in words.
- Wazza OS's updates follow your computer's proxy settings, HTTPS and SOCKS proxies included.
- Wazza OS looks for updates once an hour and checks a downloaded update once at start, so it does less work in the background.
- The update confirmation names the program that will install the update.
- A restart that some apps refused names the apps that did not come back, instead of saying they all did.
- While an update downloads, your apps keep working: their changes take effect when the update is applied or at the next start, and a failed update puts them back.
- On openSUSE Tumbleweed with SELinux, installing a Wazza OS update works: the installer's programs now sit where SELinux lets them run.
- The tarball's installer says the real reason when it refuses to install, instead of always blaming an app left open.
- Wazza OS 0.3's updater reads a release's notes up to 4096 lines of 16384 bytes, so a later release can carry its full changelog.
- Quit, a VM's Stop or Restart, and Wazza OS's restart for its update read, on demand, whether a normal Chromium tab has an Incognito or Guest window open; one opens the private question in its own words, fail-closed.
- A lab-signed file passes only on a lab machine.
- No "needs one restart" footnote under a covered release's "no restart" chip.
- Wazza OS has its own version number, 0.3, in its packages, its update notes and this guide.
- Wazza OS 0.3 can read much longer update notes, so a later version can show its full list of changes when it updates.

## MCP tools and servers

- A lane on the agent's virtio port learns its parallel from one ping at its birth.
- The MCP keeper as its own small program, asked first; Wazza OS's binary the fallback.
- A global call with under one whole second of its own bound left is refused, never given a floor of 1 s.
- A global call's wait for its rows and its run share ONE deadline, its own; past it the call is refused in words and never runs.
- One source for the words said for a refusal.
- A detached VM job's wait is a short poll with a pause holding nothing; a failed poll is asked again.
- An MCP server problem gets one notice per VM, server and Chat.
- Every loader of our own code in wazza-app-mcp reads its module whole by its own size.
- A cmd tool's invokes wait out their VM's contention; the admission types it.
- The agent's words for the learning setting say the crew playbooks are off by default, as the code is.
- Our own MCP code files are read whole by their own size, every check of their readers kept.
- A user MCP server's Repair is the person's, says true words, and a global server's Repair runs its install script again.
- Every in-process MCP request and service loop inside a panic boundary.
- One clipboard/drop connection per live VM (drops, drags and copies reach the VM they are for).
- The workspace layer refuses a hidden agent's operation by the bridge's own list.
- A hidden agent starts its own hidden agents, through its own lease.
- No fixed number of hidden agents; memory admission alone bounds every agent.
- The VM workspace MCP ends its own command-rows reads before its process ends.
- Host Chats' global MCP tools: the first tools/list carries them.
- Native's served commands' word reaches every VM Chat's server, which lists again at once, with no call, no poll, no timer and no new VM thread.
- Opening Settings reads Settings › Chats & agents › MCP servers anew.
- Every Chat, on this computer or in a VM, can manage MCP servers with Wazza OS's own tool, and the Wazza OS skill explains how.
- Chats on this computer get their VM's global MCP tools, and none of those servers runs on this computer.
- A new place for MCP servers: Settings › Chats & agents › MCP servers.
- Wazza OS keeps one list of global MCP servers and installs them into every VM.
- The global MCP servers reach every VM when it starts.
- Wazza OS's tools point agents to the guide's page about a Chat's tools.
- Agents connected through wazza-os mcp get the same start-here line and a pointer to the guide.
- The CLI and the MCP servers carry their guide: help, a help per command, and https://os-guide.wazza.ai/.
- Both MCP servers answer a THIRD identical refused call with a stop and send nothing; a changed call always goes on; a transient refusal is never stopped.
- The supervisor waits for its APP only, never for one of its own services (the app's MCP server and that server's children), so a tab whose app ended always ends.
- A studio.command run sent directly wakes the Chat's queue pull, in every form, on both servers.
- Settings › Chats & agents › Commands lists Wazza OS's shipped commands beside the person's own, read-only with a badge, and a search box filters them.
- Settings › Chats & agents › Commands, and the shipped skill's lesson.
- A command named call (cmd.call) keeps its own arguments.
- A host Chat's Wazza OS server runs cmd.<name> as ONE call and says its list changes.
- An agent's install takes every catalog app a person can install, the old-style ones asked of the registry.
- An app that is no optional catalog installation is refused as never-repeat, with what the person can do.
- An unbound app MCP wrapper binds again on a receipt change, never on a 0.5 s timer.
- A registry swap frees the registry it replaces.
- Every agent close takes force, and its schema says what unsaved work answers.

## Other fixes

- This computer's graphics row names the cause it read, a node mode that shuts every group out, never a group the account lacks.
- A host session opened before Wazza OS's server lists moved opens again in place before its next prompt.
- The surface report's decision comes through the handler's dependencies.
- A failed or cancelled helper's folded square says so and draws its mark, never "done".
- The media viewer's poster and Play here carry their test ids only on a DEBUG page.
- The Desktop gate never outlives the launch that set it.
- Add app's "Load XTerm example" fills every field of the form.
- A DEBUG build says why a command run's items wait.
- Its fallback is the dark solid ink, never a light one.

---

Page: Chats, agents and models (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html

# Chats, agents and models

A Chat is where you talk to an agent: an AI program that does the work you ask in the VM, in the app of its tab, with its files and its command line. You pick the agent and the model it thinks with, and you can switch both in the middle of a Chat without losing the conversation.

> A Chat needs a model. With the published Wazza OS, add an API key, log in with a plan you have, or sign in to a Wazza OS account first: [Sign in, plans and API keys](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/signin.html). The screenshots on this page use an OpenRouter key added in Sign in.

## Open a Chat

- **A Chat on its own**: **+** › Apps › **Chat** (*Ask any agent*), the first of the Main apps. The tab is all Chat, for questions, files and command-line work in the VM.
- **A Chat next to an app**: every app tab has its own Chat on its left ([Tabs](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/window.html#tabs)). Its agent works in that app.

A new Chat starts with the default agent and model of [Settings › Chats & agents › New Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-chats.html#new-chats). The line above the composer says what it starts on when no default is saved.

## Write to the agent

![The composer of a new Chat: the line about the default model, the box Ask anything, or @ a file or app, the plus button, the agent and model chip Hermes, and the send button](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-composer.webp)

The composer at the bottom of a Chat.

1. Type in **Ask anything, or @ a file or app…**. `Enter` sends; `Shift`+`Enter` starts a new line.
2. **+** adds files to your message (below).
3. The agent and model of this Chat; a click opens the [model window](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#choose-the-agent-and-the-model).
4. Send. While the agent answers, this button becomes **Stop**.

### Add files

![The plus menu: Add to this message, From this computer (asks first), From the VM's files (vm-1)](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-attach-menu.webp)

- **From this computer…**: your computer's file chooser opens (*asks first*: nothing is sent before you pick). The files you pick are copied into the VM for the agent and attached to your message.
- **From the VM's files…**: the Explorer opens on this Chat's VM; drag files from it onto the Chat. A Hermes Chat gets them by their path in the VM (nothing is copied); the other agents run on your computer, so each file is copied into their Chat and attached to your message.
- Or drop files from your file manager on the Chat, or paste them or an image: every way is in [Move files](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html).

### Mention a file or an app

![Typing @ in the composer lists the VM's folders: wazza_os, Documents, Music, Pictures, Templates, Videos, each with its path in the VM](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-mentions.webp)

Type `@`: a list of the VM's files and folders (and apps) opens; keep typing to narrow it, then pick one with the arrows and `Enter` or a click. The agent gets its exact path. *wazza_os* is the folder the VM shares with Wazza OS ([Files and sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files.html)).

### Slash commands

![Typing slash in the composer lists the agent's commands: /help, /model, /tools, /context, /reset, /compress](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-slash-commands.webp)

Type `/` at the start of the box: the agent's own commands. They differ per agent; for Hermes: `/help` (list the commands), `/model` (show or switch the model), `/tools` (list its tools), `/context` (message counts), `/reset` (clear the conversation), `/compress` (sum up the conversation to save room), and more down the list.

## Follow the agent's work

![Your message: Create a file named hello.txt in my Documents folder with today's date in it, then show me its content, with the retry, copy, edit and delete buttons under it](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-user-message.webp)

![The answer from OpenRouter (your key in Sign In), xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash: Thinking, a Bash row (mkdir -p ~/Documents + 2 commands) answering 2026-11-02, the message Created /home/ubuntu/Documents/hello.txt with a code block and a preview card of hello.txt, and the reply's buttons](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-answer.webp)

An agent created a file in the VM and showed it.

1. Your message. Its buttons: **retry** (ask again), **copy**, **edit** (change it and send again), **delete**.
2. Who answers: the provider and the route (here *OpenRouter (your key in Sign In)*) and the model.
3. **Thinking**: the model's reasoning, folded (click to read it). Folded, it stays folded while the model is still thinking and says it is still running.
4. A **tool** the agent used: here *Bash*, its commands and what they printed. Tools of the app, of Wazza OS and of Drive show the same way.
5. The **message**: the answer, with code blocks (copy button) and previews of files it made.
6. A **preview** of a file in the VM: click to open it larger.
7. The answer's buttons: **copy**, **copy as an image**, **retry**, **fork** (a new Chat that starts from here), **delete**.

- **Stop**: the send button while the agent works. It stops the turn; the Chat says *Stopped.*
- **Write while it works**: what you send then waits in a queue and goes when the turn ends.
- **The tab name** becomes your first message, so you find the Chat again in the tab strip and in History.
- **The context meter** (*2% context*, bottom right) shows how full the model's memory of this Chat is ([Compact a long Chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/chats.html#compact-a-long-chat)).

## Choose the agent and the model

Click the agent and model chip (bottom left of the Chat). The model window opens on **Model**.

![The model window, Model tab: Apply to This chat or Default for new chats; the Agent list (Hermes default, Prime Agent, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, each with what it runs on); Search models with 407 models; models through Wazza OS's gateway, MiMo-V2.6-Flash selected, each OpenRouter API key, yours; Thinking On Off; Provider Auto; Refresh list; Use Hermes MiMo-V2.6-Flash](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-model-window.webp)

The model window of a Chat on Hermes with an OpenRouter key. Under each agent: what it runs on (your OpenRouter key or your own keys, a plan, your Google account).

1. **Apply to**: **This chat**, **All chats** (every Chat you have open; new Chats keep their default), or **Default for new chats** (the same as Settings › New Chats).
2. The **agent** (*default* marks the one new Chats use). Under each: what it needs.
3. **Search models**: type part of a name (for example *mimo*, *claude*, *free*); the count says how many match.
4. The **models** this agent can use now, grouped by how it reaches them (*Through Wazza OS's gateway*; your plans; your custom APIs), each with who pays (*OpenRouter API key · yours*). Grey rows say why they cannot be used with this agent.
5. **Thinking** **On**/**Off**: whether the model reasons before answering (better on hard tasks, slower and costlier). Shown only for models that can.
6. **Provider**: for an OpenRouter model, **Auto (Wazza OS's routing)** or one company that serves it.
7. **Refresh list** reads the models again (after you added a key, for example).
8. **Use …** applies it. Switching keeps the conversation: the new agent reads it from the start.

![The model search with mimo typed: 5 of 388 models, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, MiMo-V2.6-Flash, MiMo-V2.6-Pro-UltraSpeed, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, each through an OpenRouter API key, yours](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-model-search.webp)

Searching *mimo*.

### The agents

| Agent | What it is | What it needs |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes | Nous Research's open agent, Wazza OS's default. Runs in the VM, works with any model. | A model: an API key, a plan login that reaches it, a custom API, or a Wazza OS account. |
| Prime Agent | Wazza OS's own agent, built in; works with any model. | The same. |
| Claude Code | Anthropic's coding agent. | Your Claude plan (Log in with Claude), or any model through Wazza OS's gateway. |
| Codex | OpenAI's coding agent. | Your ChatGPT plan (Log in with ChatGPT), or any model through the gateway. |
| Antigravity | Google's agent. Installed the first time you pick it (*not installed* until then). | Your Google account plan (Log in with Google). |

Every agent gets the same Wazza OS tools (apps, Drive, files, other agents): see [The Wazza OS MCP](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/mcp.html).

## Compact a long Chat

![The Info and compact tab: context 25.7k of 1.1M tokens, 2%; Compact the conversation with Compact now and New chat from a summary; Compact at 80k tokens with Set; Use in this chat: tokens in, tokens out, cache hit, speed, answers, paid by OpenRouter API key](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-info-compact.webp)

The model window's **Info & compact** tab.

A model remembers a limited amount of a conversation (its *context window*). The tab shows how much of it this Chat uses (*25.7k of 1.1M tokens*), and:

- **Compact now**: the agent sums up what was said and goes on with less (Hermes uses its `/compress`, Claude Code, Codex and Prime Agent their `/compact`).
- **New chat from a summary**: a new Chat that starts from a summary of this one.
- **Compact at … tokens** › **Set**: compact by itself at that size. Without it: Hermes at 50 % of the window, Claude Code by its own rule, about 23k under the window it runs its model in (the model's own, which Wazza OS tells it), Codex and Prime Agent at 80k tokens at most, and an agent on its own plan by its own rule.
- **Use in this chat**: tokens in and out, cache hits, speed, answers, and who pays. Claude Code and Codex do not report tokens: for them the numbers are Wazza OS's estimate, marked *estimated*.

## Chat settings

![Chat settings, This chat: Learning in this chat switch on, Learn from this chat now with Learn](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-settings-top.webp)

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Learning in this chat (default: on) | What this Chat teaches can become a skill ([How Wazza OS learns](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#how-wazza-os-learns)). Turn it off for a private or throwaway Chat. |
| Learn from this chat now | **Learn** reviews this Chat now instead of waiting. |
| Persona | None, or a persona (3D artist (Blender), Film director…): its skills load in this Chat, and the persona learns from it ([Personas](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/skills.html#personas)). |

![What the chat shows: Messages Unfolded, Thinking Folded, Tools Folded, Shell Folded, Previews Unfolded, Text size Default 80 percent, Font Default](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-settings-shows.webp)

| What the chat shows | Values (default in bold) |
|---|---|
| Messages | **Unfolded**, Folded, Hidden |
| Thinking | Unfolded, **Folded**, Hidden |
| Tools | Unfolded, **Folded**, Hidden |
| Shell | Unfolded, **Folded**, Hidden |
| Previews | **Unfolded**, Hidden |
| Text size | Small, **Default**, Large, or a percentage |
| Font | **Default**, System, Mono |

![Export .md .html .txt .json, Fork: hover a reply, Delete this chat](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/img/chat-settings-foot.webp)

- **Export**: the whole Chat as Markdown, HTML, plain text or JSON, saved on your computer.
- **Fork**: hold the pointer over a reply and click its fork button: a new Chat starts from there.
- **Delete this chat**: deletes the conversation for good (it asks first).

## What an agent can do

- Work in the VM: read and write its files, run commands, install command-line tools, browse the web with its own tools. A Chat in the VM runs its tools without asking each time (Wazza OS has no ask mode); the VM is its own computer, separate from yours.
- Work in its tab's app: through the app's own tools (GIMP, Blender, ONLYOFFICE, the browser…) or by looking and clicking ([Drive](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/drive.html)).
- Start other agents in other apps' tabs, at the same time ([Several agents at once](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html)).
- Reach your own computer only as you allow: it can find and read your files (below your home folder), copy them into its VM and put its results on your computer ([its file tools](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/files-move.html#a-chat-in-a-vm-tab)). These copies follow your rules in [Settings › Files & sharing](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/settings-files.html#between-this-computer-and-vms) (into the VM: allowed by default; out of it: Wazza OS asks you), and seeing or using your screen needs [Computer Control](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/computer-control.html).

## From the command line

```
$ wazza --gui chat-transcript --tab t5 --last 4
$ wazza --gui chat-model set openrouter/xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash
$ wazza --gui chat-queue list --tab t5
```

Reading a Chat, setting the default model, the queued messages: [The command line › Chats](https://os-guide.wazza.ai/cli.html#chats).


---

Page: Several agents at once (Work with agents)
Address: https://os-guide.wazza.ai/parallel-tabs.html

# Several agents at once

One Chat can hand parts of a job to other agents. An agent that works in an app gets its own tab, with that app and its own Chat: a browser for research, GIMP for an image, an editor for code. They work at the same time, in the background, while you watch any of them or keep working in your own tab.

- **What**: Visible agents, each in its own app tab; hidden agents for background work

- **Why**: Every agent has its own window, mouse and keyboard: no one waits for a shared screen

- **Who**: Anyone with a job that spans several apps

- **Limit**: Visible and hidden agents: no fixed number; past a Chat's first agent of each kind at work, no new one starts while the VM is short of memory and cannot grow, and the Chat is told why

## Why each agent gets its own tab

An agent that works an app by its window needs that window, a pointer and a keyboard. With one shared screen, agents would take turns: while one types in a form, another cannot click in its app. In Wazza OS every app tab has its own picture of its app and its own input, so each agent drives its own app at full speed, and you see each one in its tab exactly as it works. Your own tab stays yours: new tabs open in the background, and nothing an agent does changes what you are looking at.

## Two kinds of helper agents

|  | Visible agent | Hidden agent |
|---|---|---|
| For | Work in an app's window you would want to watch: research in Chromium, an image in GIMP, a document in ONLYOFFICE, code in VSCodium, a scene in Blender | Background work with no window: a web search with its own tools, a calculation, a file conversion, a summary, a check |
| Where | A new tab of that app (or an idle tab of it you already have), with its own Chat | No tab: a Chat of its own behind the scenes |
| What you see | The tab in the strip, grouped with the Chat that started it, with a badge until you look | Its progress in the Chat that started it |
| When it ends | When it answered: its tab closes and its app ends (your Chat tells it to save its file first), unless it was asked to leave the result open | When it answered |

An app that is not installed is installed first, then its agent starts (about a minute more).

Every subagent of a Chat shows there, on every harness. A harness's own subagent tools are switched off where the harness allows it (Claude Code, Codex, Hermes); where it does not, its instructions forbid them, and one used anyway still shows there: Antigravity's (*invoke_subagent*, *run_workflow*) and Prime Agent's (*rlm.spawn*). The icon under the send box counts them and is green while one works. Click one to see what it was given and its answer. An agent's own Chat shows the same icon for the agents it started.

## Ask for several agents
